subject: 21752 restoration filing sync (#3016)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature that syncs restoration filings from the new system into COLIN, with small supporting fixes for numbered-name generation and party middle names that serve the same flow.
task: When a company restoration (full, limited, limited extension, or limited-to-full conversion) is completed in the new business registry, it must also be written back to the legacy COLIN system so both records stay consistent. The legacy API should accept restoration filings and record them with the correct legacy filing type for each restoration kind. Processing a restoration should close out the company's custodial office and any current custodian. It should set the company's state to active, or to limited restoration for limited and extension filings, recording the expiry date as the event trigger date for limited ones. It should apply any name change. For registrar-approved restorations, the applicant party should be recorded with its application date as the office notification date and the notice date as its appointment date. Numbered company names and continued-in company types should be derived correctly when syncing back, and a party's middle initial should be used when no middle name is present.

subject: 23697 - fix stage1 to stage2 dissolution transition bug (#3028)
reason: A single coherent fix to the rule that decides when a business can move from stage 1 to stage 2 of involuntary dissolution, plus the feature-flag defaults that rule depends on.
task: The involuntary dissolution job is moving businesses from the first warning stage to the second stage too early or incorrectly. Right now any one completed notice counts, so an email alone can be enough even when the mailed letter never went out. Change the rule so that if an email notice exists for the business in that batch, both the email and the mailed letter must be completed before the business advances. If no email notice exists, a completed mailed letter alone is enough. Because sending letters to the mail provider over SFTP can be switched off by a feature flag, a letter that is still queued should count as done while that flag is on. Add the new flags for turning off the mail-provider and the BC Laws SFTP deliveries to the job configurations with sensible defaults.

subject: 23522-23562 continuation in workflow change (#3026)
reason: The commit reworks one feature: the staff-review workflow for continuation-in filings. It changes how the filing is submitted for review, how approval flows into payment, the review record, deletion rules and blocker rules.
task: Rework the continuation-in staff review workflow so that a filer submits a draft continuation-in for staff review directly from the draft, with no payment, and gets an email notification. The same path should handle resubmission after staff request changes. Once staff approve, the filing should go back into the filer's hands in an approved state so they can complete and pay for it. The authorization, name request and foreign jurisdiction details must stay locked to the approved values, and approval alone must no longer trigger the filer. The review record should capture the filer's contact email instead of the completing party's name, and staff should be able to search and sort reviews by it. Filings that are awaiting review, have changes requested, or are approved should block other filings on the business. Only true drafts may be deleted, and the uploaded continuation-in documents should be cleaned up on deletion.

subject: 23521 - update continuation emails (#3036)
reason: The commit is one coherent update to the wording, subjects and attachment lists of the continuation-in notification emails, with a small related tweak to the emailer test CLI.
task: Update the emails sent to applicants during a continuation into B.C. so that each stage of the process gets its own clear subject line and message. The stages are: authorization documents received, authorization updates received, changes needed, authorization approved, authorization rejected, application received, and successful continuation. Add a new email for when the authorization documents are submitted and awaiting staff review, telling the applicant that review takes up to 5 business days and what happens after approval. Approval and rejection emails should no longer list attachments, and the rejection email should no longer mention a refund. The application-received and completion emails should list the right documents depending on whether the continuation is future-effective, and should point users to My Business Registry. Also let the developer test tool for the email queue publish name request notification messages.

subject: 23819 - Continuation Application Outputs Update (#3038)
reason: A coherent update to the continuation application PDF output and the shared business-name display logic, with matching changes to the report data preparation.
task:
Update the continuation application PDF that the legal API generates so it matches the new output design. The business name at the top should show the actual registered business name once one exists, falling back to the name request name and then to the numbered-company description. Apply the same fallback to the incorporation application header and to the benefit company statement. In the continuation application section:
- Use a continuation-specific name reservation block that explains the numbered-name option for continuations.
- Drop the completing party block.
- Reword the future effective date as a sentence.
- Change the authorization text to say the authorization from the previous jurisdiction was approved.
- Lay out the previous jurisdiction details and the previous extraprovincial registration in two-column sub-titled blocks.
- Add the extraprovincial registration date to the previous registration block, formatted in the BC legislation timezone.
- Show the jurisdiction country and region names in normal case instead of all caps.

subject: 20908 Update corp data migration pipeline to work with prefect 3 and get things working again with IAs and ARs (#3040)
reason: This is mainly a dependency and tooling upgrade (Prefect 2 to 3, requirements, Makefile, README, sample env) bundled with debug prints, a batch-size tweak and a SQL script reorder, not a single behavior change a developer could locate by understanding the domain.

subject: 23744 Script to delete migrated data (#3042)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature, a batch cleanup tool that removes test-migrated corporations, along with the config and naming adjustments it relies on.
task: The corporations migration tool tags every test-imported company by appending a marker to the end of its name, so that setting should be described as a suffix rather than a prefix. Add a runnable cleanup workflow that finds BC, ULC and community-contribution companies in the business registry database whose names end with that marker and deletes them in configurable batches (number of rounds and batch size, both required to be positive). For each batch it should remove the businesses and all related data: filings, transactions, versioned history rows, comments, batch processing entries, COLIN event links and continuation-out consents. As separately toggleable options, it should also remove the matching entity, affiliation and contact records from the auth database, and clear the migration-tracking records in the COLIN extract database for the current load environment. Deletions should bypass foreign-key triggers and roll back on error, and the workflow should report progress after each round.

subject: 24153 fixes in colin sync (#3057)
reason: All changes serve one goal, making the filing synchronization from the new registry system back to COLIN reliable, across the legal API, the COLIN API and the sync jobs.
task: The job that pushes completed filings from the legal API back to COLIN keeps stalling and failing on real data, so make the synchronization robust. The legal API's endpoint for completed filings awaiting COLIN sync should use a limit and offset instead of page numbers. It should order filings by effective date, leave out epoch filings at the query level, and stop special-casing corrections. The sync job should page through results with an offset that advances only past filings it skipped or failed to sync, and stop when no filings come back. On the COLIN side, several things need fixing: business numbers with the BC prefix are truncated to their last seven digits, which breaks longer numbers, so only the prefix should be removed. Missing address region, second address line, delivery instructions or officer email should not cause errors. Filing dates should be stored as date-only values. After saving a filing, COLIN should return just the new event IDs rather than rebuilding the whole filing. Also, the job that checks COLIN for manual filings should only look at cooperatives, and the lookup for businesses missing a business number should fetch only their identifiers.

subject: 24121 colin sync for correction filing (1 to many) (#3060)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: correction filings for corporations are now synced to COLIN as several separate filings, one per changed area, along with the supporting fixes this requires.
task: When a correction filing for a BC corporation is synchronized into COLIN, it should no longer be recorded as a single generic correction. Instead, it should produce a separate legacy filing and event for each kind of change that was corrected: company name or name translations, registered/records offices, directors, and share structure or resolution dates. Each one should use its own legacy correction type. Share corrections must also add new resolution dates and end any resolution dates that were removed. Name corrections must handle reverting to a numbered company name correctly. If the correction contains none of these changes, or the entity is not a corporation, the request should be rejected with an error. Party, address and name handling must tolerate missing or empty name and address fields, so that corrections with partial data do not fail.

subject: 23958 update fe date issue (#3067)
reason: A single coherent fix to how future effective dates are worded in generated filing PDFs (amalgamation, incorporation, alteration, continuation), findable by understanding the report generation.
task: The PDF documents the legal API generates for filings are showing the wrong text for the effective date section when a filing is future-effective. For amalgamation and incorporation applications, the output shows a bare (and sometimes empty) date value instead of a full sentence stating that the amalgamation or incorporation is to take effect on the given date and time. Alteration documents always say the change takes effect when filed, even when a future effective date was chosen; they should state the future date when one applies. Also, continuation documents filed without a future date incorrectly say "the incorporation" takes effect on filing; that wording should refer to the continuation.

subject: 24085 alteration BC to ULC fee code (#3070)
reason: The commit implements one business rule: an alteration that converts a BC company to an unlimited liability company gets its own fee code when the invoice is created. The other changes are small refactors and formatting in support of that rule.
task: When a BC limited company files an alteration that changes its business type to an unlimited liability company, the legal API should charge the fee specific to that conversion rather than the standard alteration fee. When building the fee list sent to the payment service, the API should compare the business's current type with the new type requested in the alteration. If that particular type change has its own fee code configured, the API should use it, and all other alterations should keep their existing fee. Register the dedicated fee for the BC-to-ULC conversion in the filing fee configuration so that both the filing metadata and the model-level fee lookup recognize it.

subject: 24295 - Freeze all corporations when synchronizing to COLIN (#3076)
reason: A single coherent business-rule change: when filings are synchronized into COLIN, freeze every corporation type except cooperatives, gated behind a feature flag. The supporting feature-flag lookup helpers exist only to serve that rule.
task: When filings from the new registry system are written back into the legacy COLIN database, only benefit companies (and community benefit companies) currently get marked as frozen in COLIN, so other corporation types can still be edited there. Now that BC limited companies, community contribution companies and unlimited liability companies are being managed in the new system, all corporations except cooperative associations should be frozen in COLIN when their filings are synchronized. This should be controlled by the existing feature flag that enables BC/CCC/ULC support, so the COLIN API needs to be able to evaluate feature flags at runtime. When the flag is off, keep the current behavior of freezing only new or altered benefit companies. The flag should default to on for local development.

subject: 24361 - fix missing pdf continuation application (#3078)
reason: The commit is one coherent fix: when the business has no legal name (a numbered company), the receipt PDF request uses the numbered-company description so the receipt is generated and attached; the debug logging and template list tweak support that same continuation-in email fix.
task: When a numbered company (one with no legal name yet) completes a continuation in, an amalgamation or another filing, the confirmation email sent by the email notification service is missing the receipt PDF. This happens because the receipt request to the payment service is sent without a company name. Change the receipt generation so that, when the business has no legal name, it falls back to the standard numbered-company description for that business type (for example, "Numbered Limited Company"). Use the same fallback for every filing type instead of reading the name from the incorporation application. Also update the continuation-in completed email so its list of attached documents matches what is actually sent, and add temporary debug logging around the email message and the receipt request to help diagnose any remaining failures.

subject: 24051 Tombstone pipeline (first cut) (#3077)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: a first-cut migration pipeline that pulls a current-state snapshot of each corporation from the legacy COLIN extract and loads it into the LEAR database. The shared DB-init refactor and batch-setting split exist to support it.
task: In the data migration tooling, add a new batch pipeline that migrates a 'tombstone' snapshot of corporations from the legacy COLIN extract database into the new business registry database. For each unprocessed corporation of the supported BC company types, collect its current state: core business details (name, type, founding date, state, tax number, annual report info, admin freeze), registered and records offices with addresses, incorporators and directors with their roles and addresses, share classes and series, translated names, and resolutions. Clean and reshape this data, then insert it per corporation in a single transaction, running corporations concurrently in configurable batches. The batch count and batch size settings should be separate from those used by the existing corporation delete flow. The database connection setup currently inside the delete flow should become shared so both flows can reuse it. Placeholder historical filings can be stubbed out for now.

subject: 22757 - Remove Completing Party Section (#3085)
reason: A single coherent behavior change that removes the completing party section and its certification statement from several generated filing PDFs, along with the unused template parts and their registration in the report generator.
task: The PDF documents the legal API generates for business filings should no longer show the completing party. Today, the outputs for amalgamation applications, registrations of firms, changes of registration, client corrections (for both corporations and firms), and dissolutions of sole proprietorships and general partnerships include a section listing the completing party's name and mailing address. They also include a statement certifying that this person has relevant knowledge of the business and is authorized to make the filing. Remove both the section and the statement from these reports, and clean up the now-unused report pieces so the report generator no longer loads them.

subject: 24368 - Update BEN Statement in NOA (#3096)
reason: A single coherent behavior change: the benefit company statement wording in generated filing documents changes, gated behind a new feature flag.
task: The benefit company statement printed on generated business documents, such as the Notice of Articles, needs updated wording. It should say the company is committed to conducting its business in a responsible and sustainable manner and promoting one or more public benefits, instead of saying the company has purposes that include doing so. The rollout must be controllable, so add a new feature flag that is off by default. The legal API's document generation should read the flag and choose between the old and new wording when it renders the statement.

subject: 24741 cease custodian while filing putbackon (#3118)
reason: The commit is a coherent business-rule change: a put back on filing now ends any custodian appointment and removes the custodial office, reusing the custodian-ceasing logic from restoration, plus a related fix to how filing documents pick up the entity type.
task: When a business that was dissolved and placed under a custodian is put back on the register through a put back on filing, the custodian appointment stays active and the custodial office stays attached to the business. Change the filer service so that processing a put back on filing ends any active custodian role as of the filing time and removes the business's custodial office. Do this the same way a restoration filing already ceases the custodian, and share that behavior between the two filing types rather than duplicating it. Also fix the generated filing documents for alterations: the entity-type description should come from the business type given in the alteration itself, falling back to the business's current type when none is given.

subject: 23350 - notice of withdrawal outputs - focus on NoW for existing businesses (#3148)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: a generated PDF output (plus receipt effective-date behavior) for Notice of Withdrawal filings on existing businesses.
task: Staff can now file a Notice of Withdrawal against a business's future-effective filing, but the legal API has no document output for it. Add a printable Notice of Withdrawal report. It should have the usual registry header and business details block, showing the incorporation number, filed date/time, recognition date/time and retrieved date/time. Below that, add a section describing the record being withdrawn: its human-readable filing type, its filing number, and its effective date and time in Pacific time. The business details footer should not repeat the incorporation number for this report. Also, the payment receipt for a Notice of Withdrawal should always show the effective date, even when it falls on the same day as the filing date.

subject: 25038 25039 putbackoff filing (#3151)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: a new no-fee 'put back off' correction filing for corporations whose limited restoration has expired, plus the support it needs, namely a persisted per-filing ledger visibility flag and an internal lookup of expired restorations.
task: Add a new staff/system correction filing, 'Put Back Off', that returns a business to the historical state once its limited restoration period has expired. It should be available only to corporation-type entities, carry no fee, require a details description, optionally accept a court order, and appear among the downloadable documents like the existing Put Back On filing. To support an automated process that files these, the legal API needs an internal, system-only endpoint listing the businesses whose limited restoration expiry date has passed. Replace the hard-coded rule that hides admin freezes and involuntary dissolutions from the filing history with a stored per-filing visibility flag. Set the flag when a filing is saved, so those two filing types remain hidden, system callers can ask for a filing to be hidden through a request header, and the involuntary dissolution job marks its filings hidden. Existing records must be backfilled so they stay hidden.

subject: 25042 - put back off sync (#3157)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: the COLIN API now accepts a put-back-off filing for corporations, records it with its own event filing type, and sets the corporation's state to involuntarily dissolved.
task: When a registry staff member files a 'put back off' on a BC corporation in the new system, the legacy COLIN database never learns about it, so the two registries drift out of sync. Extend the COLIN-side API so it accepts this filing type for all BC company types, including benefit companies, unlimited liability companies, community contribution companies and their continued-in variants. Record each filing in COLIN under the appropriate legacy filing code. Processing it should move the corporation back to the involuntarily dissolved state (the same state used for dissolution for failure to file annual reports). It should be handled like the existing 'put back on' filing, so that it is recognized when filings are listed and retrieved.

subject: 24195 tweaks on filing queries (#3166)
reason: The commit makes one coherent change: the legal API now treats a business's most recent and previous completed filings as the ones last processed, rather than ordering by effective or filing date, and consolidates the lookups that relied on this.
task: The legal API currently decides which filing is a business's 'most recent' or 'previous completed' filing by effective date or submission date. This gives wrong answers when filings are future-effective, backdated, or still pending. Change these lookups to use the order in which completed filings were actually applied to the business's history. Use this single rule everywhere: the latest-filing summary on the business, the limited-restoration extension/conversion validation, and the firm completing-party warning check. A filing still pending should have no position in that history, so its previous completed filing is simply the latest one applied. Also fix the lookup by a specific filing so it really restricts to that filing, and stop returning a 'last modified' date in the business details response.

subject: 24479 - Tombstone pipeline - amalgamation & legal-api adjustment (#3163)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: migrating amalgamation history for tombstoned COLIN corporations, plus matching legal API changes so business documents work for those businesses.
task: Extend the COLIN-to-LEAR tombstone migration pipeline so that amalgamation history is carried over. When a migrated corporation's history includes an amalgamation application, record the amalgamation itself (date, court approval, and type: regular, vertical or horizontal) linked to that placeholder filing. Also record each amalgamating party with its role (amalgamating or holding). Foreign or extra-provincial parties should be stored by their foreign jurisdiction, name and number. Parties that are local corporations should be linked to their business record, creating or updating it so it shows as dissolved by that amalgamation. The business's current state filing should only be the filing that matches its current COLIN state event, and an existing pre-loaded business should be updated rather than skipped. The batch delete tool should also clean up amalgamation records. In the legal API, add a tombstone filing status. Businesses that carry it should read amalgamation data directly, without version history. They should show 'Not Available' placeholders for amalgamation details in business summaries and documents, and treat amalgamations before the tombstone date as imported from COLIN. Address formatting should also cope with a missing city or country.

subject: Hotfix updates (#3187)
reason: The main change is one coherent rule: COLIN only freezes a non-cooperative company when that company already exists in the new registry system, plus a closely related split of the same rollout flag for annual report reminders.
task: When the COLIN API records a filing for a BC company, corporation or unlimited liability company under the new-entity rollout flag, it currently freezes the entity in COLIN even if that business was never loaded into the new registry. Before freezing, the COLIN API should check with the legal API whether the business exists there, authenticating as a service account. It should freeze only if the business is found. Note that the check must use the business's new-system identifier, not the converted COLIN identifier. Separately, annual report reminder emails for these company types should be controlled by their own dedicated feature flag, so reminders can be enabled independently of the broader rollout.

subject: 24988 now documents temp business (#3182)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: it makes documents (receipts and filing outputs) available for notices of withdrawal filed against temporary, not-yet-incorporated businesses.
task: When staff file a notice of withdrawal against a future-effective filing for a business that does not exist yet (one still known only by its temporary registration number), users currently cannot retrieve that notice's documents. Update the legal API so that the documents list and document download work for such a notice when it is requested under the temporary business identifier. Withdrawn filings should be treated like paid filings when deciding which documents to offer. Receipts should be available for withdrawn filings. When there is no business record, the business name and type shown on the receipt and report should fall back to the business details recorded in the notice itself.

subject: 23351 - Notice of Withdrawal Emailer (#3195)
reason: A single coherent feature: when a notice of withdrawal filing completes, the email queue service sends a confirmation email with attached documents.
task: When a Notice of Withdrawal filing is completed, the business email notification service should send a confirmation email. It should say the record was successfully withdrawn and show the company name (only for existing businesses, not temporary new-business registrations), the filing and effective date and time, and the display name of the filing being withdrawn. It should also link to the business dashboard. Attach the Notice of Withdrawal document and the payment receipt. For existing businesses, send the email to the business contact from the auth service. For a temporary business, use the contact point email and the completing party's email from the withdrawn incorporation-style filing. The subject should name the business (or say numbered company) for existing businesses. The message tracking logic must also treat completed withdrawal emails like other completed-option filing emails so duplicates are detected.

subject: 25467 colin sync - effective date should be same as filing date if not future effective (#3204)
reason: The commit is one coherent change to how filings completed in the new system are synchronized back to COLIN: it sets the effective date correctly for non-future-effective filings and drops a remote lookup used when deciding whether to freeze a business.
task: When filings completed in the new business registry are synchronized back to the legacy COLIN system, COLIN currently always records the effective date sent from the legal API. For filings that are not future-effective, this causes small mismatches between the effective date and the filing date. The legal API should tell the sync process whether each completed filing is future-effective, meaning its effective date is later than its payment completion. COLIN should keep the supplied effective date only for future-effective filings and otherwise use the filing date. Also, when COLIN decides whether to freeze a business against legacy edits, it should rely on whether the filing came from the new system, rather than calling back to the legal API to check whether the business exists there; that callback and its supporting client code can be removed.

subject: 25231, 25287 - update put back off sync for limited restoration expiration and update correction output (#3205)
reason: The core change is one coherent behavior: syncing system-generated put-back-off filings for expired limited restorations from the legal API to COLIN as a state-change event; the notebook output tweak is incidental.
task: When a limited restoration expires, the system automatically files a hidden 'put back off' filing that makes the business historical. This filing currently isn't synchronized correctly to COLIN. The legal API's feed of completed filings for COLIN should tell the sync whether each filing is hidden from the business's ledger. When COLIN receives a hidden put-back-off filing, it should not create a regular filing. Instead it should record a system dissolution event, change the corporation's state to a new 'restoration expired' state, and return the new event id as the COLIN id.

subject: 22411 btr lear filing integration (#3208)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: a new Transparency Register filing type that flows through the legal API (types, fees, permissions, validation, payment corp type, history exclusion) and the payment queue handling.
task: Add support in the legal API for a new Transparency Register filing (significant individuals register) that corporations can submit in three flavours: an initial filing, a change filing, and an annual filing. All BC and continued-in corporation types (including benefit, unlimited liability and community contribution companies) should be allowed to file it, unless the business is frozen or has a pending future-effective incorporation, and each flavour should be charged the significant-individuals register fee. These filings come from the separate transparency register product, so their payments should be billed under that product's own corp type, and they should be marked as originating from that system. They should not create legal-filing entries or appear in the public feed of filings sent to other systems. When the payment service's queue listener receives payment completions for this product, it should process them like other business filings instead of ignoring them. Bump the business schemas to the version that defines this filing.

subject: 24593 Tombstone pipeline - implement conversion (exclude liquidation, invol dissolution, cont out) (#3199)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: legacy COLIN conversion events are migrated as hidden conversion filings that carry their underlying filing type, and the legal API's business summary report reads them.
task: When legacy corporations are migrated from COLIN into the new registry, their historical conversion events should come over as conversion filings rather than being skipped or force-mapped to amalgamations or incorporations. Each conversion filing should record what kind of filing it really represents, such as an amalgamation, continuation in, voluntary or unknown dissolution, full or limited restoration, or name change, and whether it changed the business state or name. These filings should be hidden from the filing history ledger, and so should involuntary dissolutions. Their effective dates should come from the conversion event, and name changes should capture the old and new corporate names. The legal API's business summary document should then use these converted records for its state changes, name changes, amalgamation details and continuation-in jurisdiction details. Alterations that change the business type (for example ULC to BC, BC to ULC, BC to CC) or the legal name should record the before and after values. Amalgamations of unknown type must be supported, and missing legacy values should show as 'Not Available' or a generic 'Dissolved' label. Also, corporations skipped because of data collection errors should be marked as failed in migration tracking.

subject: Merge feature-data-migration back to main branch (#3249)
reason: This is a feature-branch merge that rolls up several unrelated data-migration changes (in-dissolution import, notice-of-withdrawal handling, put-back-off mappings, AR reminder year, colin event ids, DB indexes, deployment comments, formatting), so it is not one coherent behavior change.

subject: 26151 - Rebase release branch and merge into main (#3251)
reason: This is a release-branch rebase/merge roll-up bundling many unrelated changes (amalgamation court approval wording, put-back-off business summary, withdrawn filing queries, notice-of-withdrawal emails, continuation-in email templates, restoration report fixes, version bumps) rather than one coherent behavior change.

subject: 25188 - court order filing added (#3203)
reason: Single coherent behavior change: court order filings move from a free staff-only fee to a per-entity-type court fee and now produce output documents (receipt, filing PDF, uploaded court order) once paid.
task: Court order filings are currently treated as free staff filings that produce no output documents, but the business wants them to be charged a dedicated court order fee for every entity type (sole proprietorships, general partnerships, cooperatives, BC companies, benefit companies, community contribution companies, unlimited liability companies, and their continued-in equivalents). Update the legal API so the fee for a court order is looked up by the business's entity type, the same way other paid filings are, instead of the flat no-fee staff code. Also, once a court order filing has been paid, the documents listing should include the filing output and a receipt like other paid filings, plus the uploaded court order file when one was attached.

subject: API/Filer - TR todo logic (#3246)
reason: The commit is a single coherent feature: it adds to-do items for Transparency Register filings to the legal API, tracks the year of each business's last annual register filing, and has the filer record that year.
task: Businesses now have to file a Transparency Register (the registry of significant individuals). Starting from a configurable program start date, the legal API's business to-do list should show register filing tasks for active businesses other than sole proprietorships, general partnerships and cooperatives. An initial register filing is due six months after incorporation for businesses founded after the program start, or six months after a restoration. An annual register filing is due two months after each incorporation anniversary. Annual tasks should appear once they are within two months of their due date, and any overdue years should also be listed. Each register task should be placed right after the annual report task for the same year, and only the first outstanding register task should be enabled. When the filer processes an annual register filing, it should record the year of the business's last annual register filing so the next due date can be calculated. Register filings should also be allowed to have an effective date earlier than their payment date, as annual reports already are.

subject: 25957 appoint_receiver_filing (#3252)
reason: The commit adds one coherent new filing type for appointing a receiver on corporations, wiring it through the filing metadata, fee codes, permissions, party roles and validation in the legal API.
task: Corporations need to be able to submit a new filing that records the appointment of a receiver to the business. Please add support for this 'appoint receiver' filing in the legal API for all BC, benefit, unlimited liability, community contribution and continued-in corporation types. It should be charged under the no-fee filing code, appear with a friendly display name and title, and be offered as an allowable filing subject to the standard business blocker checks. Receivers should be recognized as a new kind of party role on a business. The filing should go through the normal validation flow, and for now it only needs the checks the updated business schema package already provides, so bump that schema dependency to the release that defines the new filing.

subject: 26262 - change init_db importing approach (#3278)
reason: The commit only changes where an existing database-initialization helper is imported from across several jobs and queue services, a pure import refactor with no behavior change.

subject: 26189 Fix misc issue from tombstone prelim dry run & misc updates (#3275)
reason: The commit bundles several unrelated tweaks under 'misc', including a new other-currency column, widening max shares to a large numeric type, null-safe business JSON and report rendering, parameterized SQL in the data migration tool, and a placeholder jurisdiction, so it is not one coherent behavior change.

subject: 26298 - Display Historical Date instead of Effective Date (#3280)
reason: A single coherent fix: the business summary report should show, for a put-back-off filing, the day after the expiry date instead of the raw expiry date.
task: On the business summary document that the legal API generates, the state-transition history shows the wrong date for put back off filings. Today it shows the filing's expiry date. It should instead show the date the business actually became historical, which is the day after that expiry date in BC legislation time. Show it in the usual long report format (for example, "August 5, 2021") so the summary reflects when the business really transitioned.

reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: support in the legal API for a new filing type that records the end of a receivership.
task: Corporations can already file a notice that a receiver has been appointed. They now also need to be able to file a notice that the receiver is no longer acting. Add support in the legal API for this new filing type for all BC corporation types (benefit companies, limited and unlimited liability companies, community contribution companies, and their continued-in equivalents), but not cooperatives. Give it its own fee code, the same for every eligible business type. Make it available only when the business has no standard blockers. It should pass validation with schema checks only for now, like the receiver appointment filing.

subject: 26476 - Support Save and Update Consent to Amalgamate Out draft (#3300)
reason: The commit coherently introduces a new filing type (consent to amalgamate out) across filing metadata, fee codes, outputs, and authorization rules so drafts can be saved and updated.
task: Corporations need to be able to request a 6-month consent to amalgamate out of British Columbia, similar to the existing consent to continue out. Add this as a new filing type in the legal API so that drafts of it can be saved and updated. It should be available to all BC corporation types, including limited, benefit, community contribution, and unlimited liability companies and their continued-in equivalents. It should be blocked for businesses that are not in good standing or that have the usual business-level blockers. The filing should be billed under a new fee code for amalgamating out and should produce a letter of consent as an additional output. Update the shared business schema library to the version that defines this new filing.

subject: 26472 Add App-Name as new allowable header and add error handling logging that includes new header when available (#3302)
reason: The commit makes one coherent change: the legal API accepts a client-identifying request header through CORS and includes it in error logs.
task: Front-end applications calling the legal API will start sending a request header that names the calling application, but browsers currently block it because the API's cross-origin responses, including preflight replies, do not list it as an allowed header. Update the API's CORS handling so this application-name header is permitted alongside the existing authorization and content-type headers. When the API logs an HTTP error or an unexpected server exception, include the calling application's name from this header so support staff can tell which client caused the failure. If the header is missing, log the source as unknown. If the value contains anything other than letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, replace it with a placeholder rather than logging the raw value.

subject: 26487 - Support save amalgamation out draft (#3305)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: it registers a new amalgamation-out filing type in the legal API so drafts can be saved, and adds the matching type metadata, fee codes and permission rules.
task: The legal API needs to recognize a new 'amalgamation out' filing so staff can save draft filings for a BC corporation that is amalgamating into a business outside the province. Register it as a known filing type with a display title. Map it to its own fee code for all BC company types, both regular and continued-in: limited, benefit, unlimited liability and community contribution companies. Only make it available to those corporation types when the business is in good standing and has already completed a consent to amalgamate out.

subject: 25959 - Cease receiver filing
reason: The commit implements one coherent feature, the end-to-end Cease Receiver filing, covering validation, filer processing, the PDF output, and the completion email; the remaining changes are incidental lint fixes and schema version bumps.
task: Businesses that have appointed a receiver need to be able to file a Cease Receiver to end that appointment. When the filing is submitted, the legal API should reject it unless every party listed is currently an active receiver of that business. When the filing is applied to the business record, each listed receiver's role should be marked as ceased as of the time of processing. The filing also needs a printable output document that shows the business name, incorporation number and filed date and time. Once the filing completes, the business contact should get a confirmation email with that document and the payment receipt attached.

subject: Merge pull request #3336 from chenhongjing/26445
reason: Though titled as a merge, the commit is one coherent feature: carrying each corporation's legacy COLIN passcode through the migration data tool into the auth service when entities are created or affiliated, with an optional override.
task: When the corporations migration tool brings businesses over from COLIN, it should also carry across each corporation's existing passcode so that owners can still use it to manage their business in the new system. Extract the passcode along with the other corporation data, and send it to the auth service when the business entity is created and when it is affiliated to an account. For testing, add a configuration option that replaces every migrated business's real passcode with a single custom passcode. Also have affiliation happen after entity creation, and treat an 'accepted' response from the auth service's entity endpoint as success along with 'created'.

subject: 26570, 26720, 26685 Update business_details_version.py to return appropriate data for tombstone corps for offices and parties data (#3338)
reason: A single coherent fix: for businesses migrated as tombstone corps, the point-in-time office and party data falls back to current data when version history is missing for filings made after the migration placeholder filing.
task: For corporations migrated from COLIN as tombstone records, the point-in-time views of a business's offices and directors/parties come back empty or incomplete. These views are used in filing outputs, PDF reports, the business profile, and the COLIN sync of amalgamations and director changes. The cause is that migrated businesses have no version history for that data. Update the legal API so that, when a filing was made after the business's tombstone migration filing, any offices or party roles missing from version history are filled in from the business's current records. Keep honoring any director-role filter, and handle missing address fields gracefully by returning empty strings. The migration tool should also give the placeholder epoch filing it creates a transaction, so filings can be ordered relative to the migration point.

subject: 26707 - exclude NOA for comment only corrections (#3358)
reason: The commit implements one coherent feature, a 'comment only' correction flag. It is handled consistently across validation, output documents, reports, emails, COLIN sync and the COLIN API.
task: Staff need to be able to file a correction against a corporation's earlier filing that only adds an explanatory comment and changes no business data. Add a comment-only indicator to corrections. Only staff or the system may set it, and when it is set the usual data validations for corrections should be skipped. A comment-only correction must not produce a Notice of Articles. That means the document should not be listed as an available output, the correction report should not try to render changed business data, and the correction notification email should not attach a Notice of Articles. When such a correction is synchronized to the legacy COLIN system, no change-section flags should be sent. COLIN should record it as a comment-only correction based on the explicit indicator, and it should return an error if a correction ends up creating no filing at all.

subject: 27054 Update get_business_revision to return fallback data for tombstone corps (#3380)
reason: The commit is one coherent fix: the historical business lookups now fall back to the current business record when no version history exists for corporations migrated from COLIN (tombstone corps), and all callers are updated to pass the filing; the comment-only correction metadata in the migration tool is a closely related small addition.
task: For corporations migrated from the legacy registry as tombstone records, the legal API has no historical snapshots of the business before the migration point. Because of this, the business data shown for a filing (in filing outputs, generated reports and documents, and the COLIN sync endpoint) comes back empty or breaks. When no historical business snapshot exists for a filing and that filing is dated after the business's tombstone migration filing, fall back to the business's current data. The historical lookups should work from the filing itself rather than from a bare transaction reference so they can make this check. Also remove the unused lookup of business data after a filing. In the migration tool, mark legacy comment-only correction events as comment-only corrections in the filing metadata.

subject: 27072 - Consent to Amalgamation Out Emailer (#3386)
reason: Coherent feature adding a confirmation email for the consent-to-amalgamate-out filing, plus a dedicated letter-of-consent document in the legal API's report generation.
task: When a company completes a consent to amalgamate out of British Columbia, the business registry currently sends no confirmation email. Add a confirmation email to the notification service for completed filings. The email should attach the 6-month consent filing document, a letter of consent, and the payment receipt, and should go to the business contact and, when staff filed it, the optional document email from the filing. The letter of consent for amalgamation out needs its own wording, distinct from the continuation-out letter. It should state that the company was authorized to amalgamate with foreign corporations under section 284 of the Business Corporations Act, give the consent expiry date, and ask for the foreign jurisdiction's record so the company can be removed from the register. The legal API should generate this letter as the filing's output document, and completed amalgamation-out messages should be tracked for duplicate handling the same way continuation-out ones are.

subject: 26661 - Transition filing email and outputs (#3393)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: email notifications with attachments for transition filings, plus a section in the transition outputs that shows pre-existing company provisions.
task: When a company files a transition application to comply with the current Business Corporations Act, the business registry should email the business contact. When the filing is paid, send a confirmation email with the transition application and the payment receipt attached. When the filing is completed, send an email with the Notice of Articles attached. Message tracking should handle these emails the same way it handles other filing notifications. Also, the transition application document and the Notice of Articles should include a 'Pre-existing Company Provisions' section when the filing says those provisions apply. The notice-of-articles part of the transition application should use the generic company statement instead of the benefit-company-specific one.

subject: 27268 - Remove NOA text from email templates (#3419)
reason: The commit makes one coherent change to correction-filing email behavior: it hides Notice of Articles wording for comment-only corrections and suppresses emails for system-generated benefit company statement corrections, with supporting tweaks in the notebook and worker.
task: When a staff correction is comment-only, the correction emails still tell the business that a Notice of Articles is attached or will be sent, even though no such document is produced. Update the correction 'paid' and 'completed' email notifications so the Notice of Articles text only appears when the correction is not comment-only. In addition, the bulk corrections that add the benefit company statement are run by staff from a notebook, and these should not send any email to businesses. Mark those corrections with a flag in the filing header, and have the email service skip them without failing, logging that there was nothing to send. Also remove the now-unused helper in the filer service that detected system-filed filings.

subject: 27330 feat: DBC2 (#3215)
reason: A coherent feature reworking digital business credentials so that each user of a business, not just the business, has their own wallet connection and credential, with wallet attestation and access rules, plus the supporting data-model migrations.
task: Rework the digital business card feature in the legal API so that wallet connections and issued credentials belong to a specific user of a business rather than to the business as a whole. Each user should get their own record linking them to the business, created on demand when they first interact. Invitations, connection lookups, and credential issuance should all be scoped to that user. Connection states should follow the newer DID-exchange protocol (invitation sent, request received, response sent, abandoned, completed). Connections should track whether the holder's wallet has been attested, and when, using a separately configured wallet attestation credential definition. Issued credentials should keep the raw credential data, the roles the user self-attested, and the revocation date. Eligibility and role checks for who may receive a credential should go through a dedicated rules component. Existing connection and credential data must be migrated to the new per-user structure.

subject: Jobs - updated for gcp db connection (#3421)
reason: The commit is one coherent change: the three SFTP reporting jobs move their database connection to Google Cloud SQL with IAM authentication, keeping a local Postgres fallback, plus the supporting dependencies and sample config.
task: The scheduled SFTP jobs that produce the Gazette file, the ICBC report and the NUANS report connect to the business database with a plain username/password Postgres connection string. That will stop working now that the database is moving to Google Cloud. Update each job's report-generation notebooks to connect through the Cloud SQL connector using IAM-based authentication with service-account credentials whenever a Cloud SQL instance connection name is configured. When no instance name is set, they should fall back to a direct local Postgres connection. Have the notebooks load their settings from a local environment file, provide a sample environment file for each job, and pin the libraries needed for the new connection approach.

subject: 27329 feat: DBC2 Queue Service (#3376)
reason: The commit changes one behavior coherently: the digital credentials queue service now finds credentials through each business user's own active wallet connection instead of a single business-level connection, and revokes or replaces every credential rather than just the first.
task: Business digital credentials are now issued per business user, each through their own wallet connection, rather than through a single connection for the whole business. Update the digital credentials queue service to match this model. When a business event happens (business number assigned, name change on a change of registration, voluntary or administrative dissolution, put back on, or an administrative revocation), it should find every issued, unrevoked credential held through each user's active connection and revoke or reissue all of them, not just the first one. When replacing a credential, issue the new one to the same business user before deleting the old record, so the user's connection is not lost.

subject: 27115 - Create Amalgamated Out Business Summary Output (#3418)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: it shows amalgamation-out details in the business summary document and fixes the related filing-status and consent-document behavior.
task: When a BC company has amalgamated out to another jurisdiction, its business summary PDF should include an 'Amalgamation Out Information' section. The section should show the new jurisdiction (region and country names, or just the country when the region is federal), the business name in the new jurisdiction, and the effective date. The business details header for such a historical company should read 'Amalgamation out on <date>' after its state. Amalgamation-out and consent-to-amalgamate-out filings should be treated as filings without a legal output, like their continuation-out counterparts, in the filing document listings. The unused 6-month consent filing PDF should no longer be generated or attached to the consent notification email, which should only carry the letter of consent.

subject: remove pubsub audience check (#3080)
reason: A single coherent behavior change: it removes the push-subscription token verification (audience and service-account email check) from the auth queue worker and the account mailer worker, along with the now-unused shared helper and its configuration.
task: The auth queue listener and the account mailer listener currently reject incoming Pub/Sub push messages unless the bearer token carries the expected audience and comes from an allowed, verified service-account email. This check is causing legitimate pushes to be refused and is no longer wanted. Remove the token verification so both workers accept push deliveries directly. Also delete the shared verification helper and drop the audience and allowed-email settings, including their secret-vault entries, from both services.

subject: 21536 - Approval/rejection review (#3079)
reason: The commit is a single coherent feature: refund approvers can see pending EFT short name refunds and approve or decline them, with related display and routing fixes.
task: On the EFT short name details page in the account management web app, staff with a new refund-approver role need to review refund requests that are pending approval. Replace the 'no refund initiated' message with a table of pending refunds for the short name whenever any exist. Each row should show who initiated the refund, the comment, the CAS supplier number, the refund amount with a link to the refund detail page, and Approve and Decline buttons that only approvers can see. Declining should open a confirmation dialog with an optional reason. Both actions should update the refund's status through the payment API and then refresh the short name's payment history. The read-only refund detail page should show who declined the refund, when, and the reason given, and the refund detail route should be fixed so it loads the correct refund identifier instead of the short name identifier.

subject: 23647 - Update Continuation Authorization Staff Review (#3088)
reason: A single coherent UI feature change to the staff continuation authorization review page: it relabels the jurisdiction section, swaps the authorization date for a downloadable unlimited liability corporation affidavit, adds a contact information card, and retitles the review section.
task: Update the staff review page for continuation-in authorization applications to match the revised design. Refer to the business's prior jurisdiction as the "Previous Jurisdiction" rather than the "Home Jurisdiction" throughout, and drop the redundant "in Home/Foreign Jurisdiction" suffixes from the field labels. Rename the authorization documents field to "Proof of Authorization" and stop showing the authorization date. When the applicant uploaded an unlimited liability corporation affidavit, show it as its own downloadable item in that section. Add a new card showing the applicant's contact email and phone (or "[Unknown]" when missing). Finally, give the review result section a standard card header titled "Authorization Review", and label the decision dropdown "Authorization Decision".

subject: 19182 - Changes to pad invoice email to consider credits (#3130)
reason: A single coherent feature: the pre-authorized debit invoice notification now accounts for account credits when stating the amount to be withdrawn, with a matching subject line update.
task: The email we send to pre-authorized debit (PAD) account holders after their daily transactions are processed currently says the full transaction total will be debited from their bank, even when the account has credits that offset part of it. Update the account mailer so the notification breaks down the amount: show the transaction total, show any account credits applied (only when there are credits), and show the net amount that will actually be charged. The debit warning sentence should state that net amount instead of the gross total. The net amount is the transaction total minus the credit total, and the message should still work if the payment service doesn't send a credit value. Also reword the email subject to read as 'Your PAD Transaction Details' under the usual BC Registries and Online Services prefix.

subject: 17950 - Display a credit being applied in transactions list (#3128)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: refunded or credited PAD and online-banking transactions get an extra 'account credit' entry in the account transactions list, plus a matching status tooltip; the version bump and formatting changes are incidental.
task: In the account transactions list, when a pre-authorized debit or online banking transaction has been refunded as a credit to the account, users currently can't see when that credit was applied. For each paid, refunded, or credited transaction of those payment types that has a refund amount and refund date, show an additional row representing the credit. That row should appear as paid, use 'Account Credit' as the payment method, show the refund amount, and be dated on the refund date, and the list should stay ordered newest first. Transactions with a credited status should also show an info tooltip explaining that the amount has been credited to the account used for the transaction, similar to the existing refunded tooltip. In addition, the account's credit information should be loaded as soon as the transactions page opens, not only when the user switches accounts.

subject: 24004 - update paymentMethodChanged when settings bcolInfo, fix error handling (#3132)
reason: The commit is a coherent fix to BC Online (BCOL) account linking in the auth web UI: it marks the payment method as changed once BCOL credentials are verified in account settings, and it shows readable error messages when the backend nests the error text inside a structured object.
task: In the account settings payment section, when a user switches to BC Online and successfully links their BC Online credentials, the screen does not recognize that the payment method has changed, so the user cannot save the change. Update it so that a successful BC Online login in settings is treated as a pending payment method change. Also, when linking a BC Online account fails with a conflict or bad-request response, the backend now sometimes returns the error message as an object containing a detail field rather than plain text. Every place in the auth web app where users enter BC Online credentials (account creation, the payment method selector, and account settings) should show the detail text when it is present and otherwise fall back to the plain message.

subject: 22468 - Launch Tiles (#3134)
reason: A single coherent feature: generalize the staff dashboard's feature tile into a reusable launch-tile layout and add a feature-flagged Document Record Service tile linking to the documents UI.
task: On the staff dashboard in the account web app, replace the standalone involuntary dissolution card with a reusable 'launch tile' layout. Each tile shows an icon, a title, a short description and an action button, and tiles sit side by side in a two-column grid. Re-implement the existing involuntary dissolution entry as one of these tiles, still controlled by its existing feature flag. Add a second tile, 'Document Record Service', that lets staff create or search document records by opening the separate documents UI, whose address comes from a new environment setting. Show this new tile only when a new feature flag for document record lookup is turned on, so the service can be rolled out gradually.

subject: 24170 - Dealer Staff Review Updates (#3145)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature that extends staff review and access-request handling of qualified supplier applications to home dealers; the launch tile layout tweak and version bump are incidental.
task: When BC Registries staff review a manufactured home Qualified Supplier access request from a home dealer, the review page should show the dealer's business location address, just as it already does for home manufacturers. Dealer applications send this address under a different field than manufacturer applications, so the review screen must handle either one. Also, the product description for the Home Dealers supplier type should list 'Transfer due to Sale or Gift' as an allowed activity. The dealer access requirements should add a new condition: all filed documents are kept for 7 years, and on request a copy or certified copy (such as the Bill of Sale or other signed forms) is provided within 7 business days at the fee set by the Registrar.

subject: 24383 - Remove FAS-UI widget (#3146)
reason: The commit removes one embedded feature, the fee accounting widget, from the auth web app and drops its dependency. That is a coherent behavior change, not just a routine dependency bump.
task: The staff side of the account management web app currently embeds the fee accounting system's search widget (routing slip lookup) by pulling in that application as a bundled package. Remove this embedded widget and every place the app wires it up or renders it. Staff should use the standalone fee accounting application for that work. Drop the package dependency so the app no longer ships the extra code and its outdated transitive libraries. Update the CI build to the newer Node runtime now that the old package no longer pins the app to an older one.

subject: 23652- Allow users to edit mailing address (#3153)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: regular account members can now edit an account's mailing address. It adds a dedicated backend endpoint, a permission, and front-end wiring.
task: Regular members of an account (not just account administrators) should be able to update the account's mailing address from the account info settings page. Today, address changes go through the general account update, which only admins may use, so non-admin members see a message that the account info is incomplete and that an administrator must fix it. Add a separate way to save only the mailing address. It should allow account members, admins and staff, record the address-change activity as before, and be granted through a new change-address permission for the regular member role. In the UI, saving the address section should use this new path independently of saving the account name and details. The incomplete-info warning should always invite the user to update the missing details themselves.

subject: 23620 - Add in year filter (#3162)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: account transaction history now defaults to a one-year date range so the page loads faster, and the date filter UI reflects that default.
task: Large accounts take a long time to open the transactions page in account settings because it loads the full transaction history. When the page opens, preset the date range filter to the last year, from one year ago through tomorrow, so only recent transactions are fetched. The date picker should open already showing that range, and the date filter field should read '1 Year' instead of being blank when no custom range has been picked. Make sure opening the page triggers only one transaction search, not an extra unfiltered load followed by the filtered one. Also throttle repeated searches so rapid filter changes don't flood the payment service.

subject: 23620 - Small fixes (#3164)
reason: The commit is one coherent fix to how the transactions table's date filter shows and tracks the default one-year range versus a custom or cleared range; the only extra change is a version bump.
task: On the account transactions page, the date filter field always shows '1 Year' whenever no custom range is picked, even after the user clears the filter and no date restriction is actually applied. Change this so the field shows 'Custom' when the user has chosen a date range, '1 Year' only when the built-in default one-year window is really in effect, and stays blank once the filters are cleared. When the default one-year window is applied, it should count as an active filter so that clearing filters works on it. The date picker should also start out in a state that matches this initial default range.

subject: 24695  - EFT Warranty - Add in Supplier Site (location in AP) EFT refund screen (#3167)
reason: A single coherent feature: capturing, displaying, and editing the CAS supplier site for EFT short names and their refunds in the staff UI.
task: Finance staff processing EFT refunds need to record the supplier site (the location within accounts payable in CAS) in addition to the supplier number, since a refund cannot be issued without both. On the refund request screen, add a required supplier site field alongside the supplier number, include it in the refund submitted to the payment service, and show it when the refund is viewed read-only. Also add a supplier site column to the short name's refund history table. On the short name details page, display the stored supplier site (or N/A when absent) with an edit action that opens the same financial-detail dialog used for the supplier number, letting staff enter a value that is saved back to the short name.

subject: 21429 - staff account search for members (#3169)
reason: The commit adds a single coherent feature: staff account search can filter accounts by their active members and can optionally return member details with each result.
task: Staff using the account search in the auth API need to find accounts by the people who belong to them. Add an optional member search term that limits results to accounts with at least one active member whose last name, first name, or username matches the text, ignoring case. Also add an optional flag that, when set, returns each matching account's member list with its results so staff can see who belongs to each account. Leave out the account back-reference and the users' contact details from that list. When neither option is given, the search should behave exactly as it does today.

subject: 24334-EFT refund fixes (#3174)
reason: The core of the commit is a coherent set of fixes to the staff EFT short-name refund workflow: a separation-of-duties rule on approvals and prefilling the new-refund form; the capitalization and column-width tweaks are minor noise.
task: In the staff screens for EFT short-name refunds, a staff member should not be able to approve a refund that they initiated themselves. Disable the approve action for any pending refund whose initiator matches the currently logged-in user, compared case-insensitively. Also, when staff start a new refund for a short name (not viewing an existing one), prefill the contact email and the CAS supplier number and site from the short name's saved details, so staff don't have to re-enter them.

subject: 24491 - EFT Instructions download update (#3175)
reason: The commit makes one coherent change: the EFT instructions PDF in the account UI is now fetched from the payment API's documents endpoint instead of a static file server, with the version bump only incidental.
task: In the account management web app, the download for electronic funds transfer (EFT) payment instructions currently pulls a static PDF directly from the public file server. Change it so the PDF is requested from the payment API's document retrieval endpoint, asking for the EFT instructions document type. This keeps the instructions centrally managed by the payment service. Remove the old direct file-server download path, and keep the downloaded file's name and loading/error behaviour the same for users.

subject: 24811 - Remove transaction counts from transaction table (#3178)
reason: The commit is one coherent behavior change: the account transactions table stops showing a total record count and pages forward on a has-more indicator instead, with the export limit message updated to match; the version bump and whitespace edits are incidental.
task: The account transactions list currently asks the payment service for a full total count on every search, which is slow for accounts with many transactions. Change the transaction history view so it no longer requests or displays a total count. The heading should no longer show the number of results, and the pagination footer should show only the current page number instead of an 'x–y of N' range. Paging forward should rely on the payment service saying whether more results exist. Also update the CSV export error message so it says the maximum record limit is 100,000 instead of 60,000.

subject: 24651 - updates for contact_centre_staff KC group (#3181)
reason: The commit makes one coherent authorization change: the auth API gets a new contact centre staff role plus fine-grained view permissions and enforces them across its staff-gated endpoints.
task: We are creating a new contact centre staff group in Keycloak so call-centre agents can help customers without holding full staff privileges, and the auth API needs to honour it. Users in this group should be treated as staff when the API checks access to a business or entity, and when it decides whether the current user counts as staff. Also add separate fine-grained permissions that the group can carry: searching the staff task queue, viewing a single task's details, viewing accounts that are pending activation through director invitations, and viewing an account's activity log. Grant access to each of those operations when the user has the matching permission, not only when they have the full staff role. Public users who hold the staff 'view accounts' permission should also see full account search results instead of the status-only view.

subject: Move staff check above GOV ACCOUNT USER (#3183)
reason: The commit is one coherent fix: staff users who also hold the government account user role are classified as staff, and that conflicting role is taken away from them.
task: Staff users who also belong to the government account user group are being treated as government account users. This gives them extra permissions they should not have. When the auth API works out a user's type from their login token, the staff role must win over the government account user role. Also, when a user's profile is created or updated after login and their token shows both the staff role and the government account user role, remove them from the government account user group in the identity provider (Keycloak) and log that it happened.

subject: 24658 Implement Staff Search by Filing ID (#3186)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: staff can search by a numeric filing number on the staff dashboard, which resolves to the owning business and links to it.
task: Staff currently can only search for an existing business on the staff dashboard by incorporation or registration number. Extend that search box so staff can also enter a purely numeric filing number. When a filing number is entered, look the filing up through the legal API's filing search, find the business it belongs to, and show it in the search result. Skip the full business lookup for temporary (not yet incorporated) businesses. Show the searched filing number in the results table, and when staff click through to manage the business, pass the filing number along to the business dashboard so it can open that filing. Also update the wording to cover the new option: the prompt, the field label and example hint, the validation and 'no match' messages, the results column header (now a generic 'Number'), and the action that leads to the business (now 'Manage Business'). Clear any previous business or filing search state before each new search, and don't apply business-number formatting to numeric filing input.

subject: 21131 - Basic STRR tile add to auth-web for account creation (#3187)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature, the Short-Term Rental Registry product tile in the account UI (product enum, display name, transaction filter, and product card text), plus minor migration doc tweaks.
task: Add the new Short-Term Rental Registry as a product that users can select when creating or managing their account in the account management web app. The product card should explain that it lets users register a short-term rental property, a platform service provider, or a strata-titled hotel or motel with the province, and manage and renew those registrations. It should also show a fee note saying a statutory fee applies plus a $1.50 service fee, with a light divider separating the description from the fee information. The product should also appear under its full name wherever products are listed, including as a filter option in the account's transaction history table.

subject: 24920 - Redirect to new BRD based on FF and Query Param (#3192)
reason: A single coherent feature: the account dashboard route redirects to a new business registry dashboard when a feature flag is on, unless a query parameter opts out. It also adds the supporting configuration URL and flag definition.
task: We are rolling out a new standalone business registry dashboard and want users who open their account dashboard in the authentication web app to be sent there instead. Gate this redirect behind a new feature flag so it can be enabled gradually. Also let users or links bypass it with a query parameter so the existing dashboard stays reachable. The new dashboard's base URL should come from environment configuration, alongside the other external application URLs.

subject: 25143 - remove product / add previously approved product support (#3200)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: account admins or staff can remove a product subscription, and if they later re-request a product that staff had already approved for that account, it is approved again automatically.
task: Account administrators and staff should be able to remove a product from an account through the auth API. Removing a product should deactivate the account's subscription to it rather than delete it, and if the subscription was still waiting for staff review, the open or on-hold review task should be discarded. If the account later requests the same product again and staff had previously approved it, the request should be approved automatically by reactivating the existing deactivated subscription, so the account does not go through review a second time. Also move the check that rejects a malformed organization ID on the product subscription endpoints into a shared validation step that returns the standard error format.

subject: 24576 - Updates to NSF messaging (#3207)
reason: The commit is one coherent change: suspended-account (NSF) messaging now surfaces the bank's returned failure reason across the suspension alert and the unlock flow, with supporting data plumbing and copy updates.
task: When a pre-authorized debit payment fails and an account is suspended for insufficient funds, users currently see only a generic 'suspended for a failed payment' message and have no idea why the bank rejected it. Update the account web app so the error reason returned by the payment service with the outstanding NSF invoice summary is carried through and shown to the user. It should appear both in the account-suspended banner and on the first step of the unlock/payment flow, for example: 'Returned system error message: <reason>'. Also refresh the related wording and styling: use a stronger red alert icon and color for the suspension notice, and show the suspension date in a human-readable 'Month DD, YYYY' format. Make the unlock page header match the 'Your Account is Suspended' header with an 'Important' callout asking the user to complete the payment steps, refer to the 'PAD agreement' rather than 'PAD terms' in the fee description, and use a single account settings subtitle that mentions managing settings, team members and viewing transactions.

subject: 24648 - contact_centre_staff role fixes (#3210)
reason: The commit is one coherent permission fix that limits what contact centre staff can see and do in the staff-facing auth web UI (terms acceptance, government account review actions, staff dashboard sections).
task: Contact centre staff should get a read-only, limited view of the staff tools in the account management web app. When a contact centre staff member opens a product's terms of service, they should not be offered the checkbox to accept the terms on the account's behalf. In the staff review of a pending government account, the extra action shown for government-type accounts should be hidden from users who lack permission to edit users.
