On the staff dashboard, the two top search/launch panels and the dev/test safe email list panel should only be shown to staff who are permitted to see those launch areas, so contact centre staff no longer see them.

subject: EFT - NSF / Outstanding balance flow fixes (#3215)
reason: A single coherent behavior change: the outstanding-balance payment request now optionally asks the payment API to include invoices of all statuses, enabled from the outstanding balances screen but not from the account-unlock (NSF) flow.
task: When an EFT account holder pays off their outstanding balance from the outstanding balances screen (for example while switching payment methods), the payment created through the payment service should cover invoices in every status, not just the default subset. The account-unlock flow for frozen accounts (NSF) should keep its current behavior and only cover the default invoices. Make the account web UI's outstanding-balance payment request able to optionally signal to the payment service that all invoice statuses should be included, and turn this on only for the outstanding balances screen.

subject: 25471 - Download Receipt in Transaction Table (#3240)
reason: The commit adds a single coherent feature, a receipt download column in the account transactions table. It is backed by a new call to the payment API's receipt endpoint.
task: Account users viewing their transaction history in the account settings should be able to download a PDF receipt directly from the transactions table. Add a new downloads column, shown by default in both the standard and extended (staff) views. For transactions that are completed or paid, the column should show a clickable PDF receipt link. Clicking it should request the receipt from the payment service on behalf of the user's current account, passing the transaction's creation date as the filing date. The returned PDF should be saved to the user's machine with a filename that includes the transaction identifier.

subject: 25223 - Manage EFT to pay web, remove manage eft from auth (#3246)
reason: The commit makes one coherent product change: it moves EFT short-name management out of the auth web app into the separate payment web app, removing the old screens and pointing staff to the new location.
task: Staff management of electronic funds transfer (EFT) payments, including viewing bank short names, linking short names to accounts, viewing short-name details, and seeing EFT-enabled accounts, now lives in a dedicated payment web application. Remove these EFT management screens, their supporting tables, lookups, dialogs and routes from the account management web app. Wherever staff previously opened EFT management, send them to the corresponding page in the payment web application instead. Add a configurable base address for the payment web application, alongside the other external web app addresses, so each environment can point to the right deployment.

subject: 25550 - Remove BCOL if feature flag is toggled and payment method i… (#3247)
reason: The commit is mainly one coherent feature: a feature-flagged phase-out of BC Online as a payment option in account settings, with a warning when switching away from it; a few minor tweaks ride along.
task: We are phasing out BC Online as a payment method, controlled by a new feature flag. When the flag is on, accounts not currently paying through BC Online should no longer see it as a payment option, either in the account payment method settings or in the payment options offered when requesting products. Accounts still on BC Online keep seeing it. When such an account picks a different method, show an alert explaining that once they save, BC Online will no longer be available to them. Also make sure the product and payment settings page re-renders properly after switching accounts, so a user who moves from a regular member account to an admin account does not see the page stuck as disabled.

subject: 25746 & 25895 - Add in handling for multiple users changing product / payments & bug fixes (#3244)
reason: The core of the commit is one coherent behavior change: detecting concurrent edits by other users to an account's products or payment method before saving. The extra bits are small related fixes such as the outstanding-balance redirect and typo corrections.
task: On the account settings page for products and payment methods, two account admins can edit at the same time and silently overwrite each other's changes. Before saving a product subscription change or a payment method change, the auth web app should re-fetch the account's current products and payment method from the server. If either differs from what the user originally loaded, the save should be aborted and a 'Conflict Detected' message shown saying another user has updated the product/payment. The page should then refresh to the latest products and payment method and exit edit mode. The unsaved-payment-method-change flag should also be tracked as account (organization) state rather than user state. Separately, the outstanding balances page should only send the user back when the total amount due, statements plus invoices, is zero, not just when invoices are zero.

subject: 25595 - Add More Payment Error Handling to Create/Update Org (#3265)
reason: The commit is one coherent change: payment-account errors raised while creating or updating an organization are now passed through the auth API to the account UI with more detail and readable formatting.
task: When creating or updating an account fails because the payment service rejects the payment account setup, users currently see a vague or empty error. The payment service reports errors in several shapes, using different fields for the error code and its description. The auth API should pick up whichever code and description fields are present, and include the detail in its error response for account creation and update. The account payment-method settings screen should then show a clear error for both conflict and bad-request failures, with a title and the error code plus detail on separate lines. Any upper-case, underscore-separated codes should be converted into readable title-case words.

subject: 25704 - Add org types for readonly staff (#3270)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: it adds two new staff account types for read-only staff and blocks ordinary account creation from using any staff type, with a clearer permission error.
task: We need to support two new kinds of read-only staff accounts in the authentication service, one for Maximus staff and one for Contact Centre staff, alongside the existing staff and Service BC staff account types. Seed these new account types in the database and widen the account-type code column if needed so the longer codes fit. Like the existing staff types, users must not be able to create accounts of these types through the normal account creation flow. When someone tries to create an account with any staff type, reject it with a clear 'insufficient permissions' error instead of the generic invalid-input error. Also make sure the public account type is recognized as a known account type in the service.

subject: Add in some org logging (#3274)
reason: A single coherent observability change: the organization ID is passed down the affiliation-details lookup path so failures in the parallel calls to source services are logged with the org they concern.
task: When the auth API fetches details for an organization's affiliated businesses and name requests, it calls the source services in parallel. If one of them is down or returns an error, the resulting error log does not say which organization the request was for, which makes failures hard to trace. Change this so the organization ID is carried through that lookup and included in the error log messages for both the 'no response' and 'error response' cases. Keep the existing behavior of reporting the service as unavailable.

subject: Migration for org default (#3286)
reason: The commit is one coherent business-rule change that retires basic accounts in favour of premium. It makes premium the default account type, always converts basic requests to premium, drops premium-only product restrictions, and simplifies the allowed payment methods.
task: We are retiring the basic account tier in the auth API, so premium should now be the default account type and basic should no longer be the default. Any new account requested as basic should always be created as premium, without depending on a feature toggle. Remove the toggle-based checks that held back premium-only products and limited the payment methods basic accounts could use. Online banking should be one of the standard payment methods available to all regular account types.

subject: 25249 - Add/remove Contact Centre Staff and Maximus Staff (#3276) (#3291)
reason: The commit implements one coherent feature: keep identity-provider staff group membership in sync when users join or leave contact centre and Maximus staff accounts, and stop a user from belonging to more than one such staff account, with matching UI error handling.
task: When a team member's membership in a Maximus staff account or a contact centre staff account becomes active, the auth API should add that user to the matching staff group in the identity provider (Keycloak). When the membership becomes inactive, the user should be removed from that group. A user may only belong to one active staff account of these types, so approving a membership for someone who already has an active one should be rejected with a clear error. The stored type code for contact centre staff accounts should also be shortened to a new canonical value, and existing data migrated to it. In the account team management screen, approving a member should show a loading state and display an error dialog with the server's message if the approval fails.

subject: 26014 - auth-api permissions updates for staff / external staff users (#3287)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: read-only access and permission handling for staff and external staff users, plus small supporting fixes for boolean query parameters.
task: Introduce a distinct read-only external staff role (used by contact centre and Maximus staff) that replaces the old contact centre staff role. Today that role is treated as full staff, so external staff need their own definition. External staff should be able to view any account's details, login options, members, products (including hidden ones), activity logs and business authorizations without being a member of the account. Viewing pending member invitations should be allowed for staff or for anyone holding a dedicated 'view members' pending invitations' role. Add a way for the membership permissions lookup to optionally return all of a staff or external staff user's permissions: on top of the normal membership-based actions, include the actions granted by the type of each active staff organization they belong to, and seed the action lists for the staff, contact centre staff and Maximus staff organization types. Also fix boolean query parameters such as 'include members' so the string 'false' is read as false instead of true.

subject: 26272 - use businessid from query string (#3296)
reason: A single coherent fix: the business profile page can now load the business from an identifier in the URL query string when the browser session has no stored business identifier.
task: When a user opens the business profile page in the account management web app directly, for example from a link in another application or in a new tab, the page currently fails to load the business. That happens because it relies only on a business identifier previously saved in the browser session. Allow the business identifier to be passed as a query parameter in the page URL, and use it as a fallback whenever the session has no stored business. The routing should pass this parameter through to the profile page, and the business loading logic should accept it, still preferring the session value when one exists.

subject: Add in App-Name to headers (#3298)
reason: The core change is one coherent feature: every outgoing HTTP request from the account management web app now carries a header naming the calling application, with the name injected at build time; the remaining edits are incidental noise.
task: Backend services such as the auth API and the payment service need to know which front-end application sent each request, for logging, analytics and troubleshooting. Update the account management web app so that every outbound API call carries a header identifying the calling application. The value should be the app's configured display name, taken from the project's package metadata and baked in at build time, not hard-coded. While there, make the loading of product payment methods tolerate an empty response from the codes lookup without throwing.

subject: 26014 - permission fixes (#3304)
reason: The commit is one coherent permissions fix: it grants contact-centre staff missing staff-dashboard views and adds a dedicated role that lets users reset another user's two-factor authenticator without being an account admin.
task: Contact-centre staff in the auth system cannot see some sections of the staff dashboard they need. Give that staff membership type permission to view account invitations, pending review tasks, and suspended accounts, and make the change reversible. Support staff also need to reset a user's one-time-password authenticator when that user is locked out. Add a new dedicated role for this, and let holders of that role call the reset-authenticator endpoint. Holders of the role should bypass the usual check that requires the caller to be an admin, coordinator, or staff on the user's account; everyone else should keep the existing authorization check.

subject: 15674 - Enhancements to the daily PAD invoice email (#3310)
reason: A single coherent enhancement to the daily pre-authorized debit invoice notification: new content fields, a deep link to the account's transactions page, and contact details.
task: Improve the daily pre-authorized debit (PAD) invoice email that the account notification mailer sends to account members. The email should open by confirming that recent transactions happened on the account, naming the account number and the account name with its branch. It should then show the transaction date and the invoice reference number, which arrives in the invoice-created event. Replace the generic login link with a link that opens the transactions page under that account's settings in the account web app, so members can review the details directly. End the email with a contact block for the Business Registry at BC Registries and Online Services, listing the toll-free number, the Victoria office number and the support email address.

subject: 26556 - Add in user / membership row on API key creation (#3327)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: when an API key is created for an account, a matching user record and an admin membership are now created for the gateway service account. These new members are also hidden from the account's member listing.
task: When an account requests API access keys through the API gateway, the auth API should also register the gateway's service-account identity as a user in our system. That user should get an active administrator membership on the account, so API calls made with the key are tied to a real member of that account. Look up the service account from the identity provider by its generated client name. Do not create a duplicate user or membership if one already exists, and put the behaviour behind a feature flag that is on by default. These API-gateway users must not show up in the account's list of team members. Work out the per-environment client name (with a sandbox suffix for non-production) in one shared place, and use it both for building the identity-provider client and for this lookup.

subject: 26547 - feature remove minio from auth api (#3329)
reason: The commit is one coherent infrastructure-backed behavior change: the auth API's document storage (affidavit uploads and signed URLs) moves from MinIO to Google Cloud Storage, along with matching config and dependency updates.
task: The auth API currently stores account documents, such as affidavits uploaded during account setup, in a self-hosted MinIO object store. As part of the move to Google Cloud, these documents should be stored in a Google Cloud Storage bucket instead. Keep the existing behavior: the front end asks for a pre-signed upload URL for a file and then uploads directly to it, and staff or users viewing an affidavit get a time-limited signed download link. The bucket should come from a single environment setting rather than the old MinIO endpoint and credentials. All MinIO configuration and the MinIO client dependency should be removed.

subject: Auto approval for SANDBOX so BCEID don't need staff approval (#3358)
reason: A single coherent business-rule change: a configuration toggle that lets BCeID users skip staff review when they join or create organizations in the sandbox environment.
task: In the sandbox environment, BCeID users should not have to wait for staff to approve them before they can use their accounts. Add an environment-level setting to the authentication API that turns off the staff-review requirement for BCeID users. This must be an environment setting, not a feature flag, because production and sandbox share the same feature-flag service. When the setting is on, a BCeID user who creates a regular or extra-provincial organization should not be sent to staff review just because they have no approved affidavit. Likewise, an unverified BCeID user accepting an invitation as an administrator should go through the normal approval flow instead of staff review. When the setting is off (the default), behavior stays as it is today.

subject: Remove loading complete before sbc-common-components SbcHeader completes requests (#3357)
reason: The commit makes one coherent fix: the app shell no longer syncs the user and marks loading complete on startup before the shared header finishes its own requests, and it removes the legacy global store that only existed for that loading flag.
task: When a user returns to the account management web app with an already synced session, the app shell syncs the user's details itself and flags the page as finished loading. This happens before the shared common header has completed its own user and account requests, so pages can render with incomplete user state. Stop the app shell from doing this startup sync and early loading-complete signal, and leave that work to the shared header. Also remove the old legacy state store and its libraries, which only held the header refresh counter and the loading flag. Remove the related build aliases as well.

subject: 27099 - Fix HTTP_ORIGIN issue for API users (#3360)
reason: The commit is mainly one fix: when an affiliation invitation is created by an API caller that sends no browser origin header, the auth API now builds invitation links from the configured web application address instead of a hard-coded 'localhost'.
task: When an API gateway client creates a business affiliation invitation through the auth API, the request usually has no browser origin. The links in the invitation email then point to 'localhost', so recipients cannot act on them. Change the invitation flow to fall back to the configured public URL of the registry web application when no origin is supplied, and make sure that setting has a value in the test configuration. Also fix the user settings response schema so that the optional additional label on a settings entry is declared as a property of that entry rather than sitting outside it.

subject: 27100 - fix enum referencing error (#3371)
reason: The commit only renames an enum member and updates its references; the stored value and behavior stay the same, so it is a pure rename rather than a behavior change.

subject: 22263 - EFT Refund AP Job Implementation (#1719)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: the accounts-payable job now produces and uploads payable files for approved EFT short-name refunds, backed by a new disbursement-tracking field on the refund record.
task: Approved refunds for electronic funds transfer (EFT) short names are never paid out right now. Extend the nightly accounts-payable job so it picks up approved EFT refunds with a positive amount that have not been sent yet and writes them in batches into a CGI accounts-payable file uploaded over SFTP. Each refund should be paid by EFT to the refund's own CAS supplier number rather than a single configured vendor, with its own configurable supplier location and distribution account, and should carry a comment line combining the short name and the refund comment. Track a disbursement status on each EFT refund, and set it to uploaded once the refund is included in a file so it is not sent twice.

subject: 20787 - allow specific action overrides (#1763)
reason: The commit is one coherent change: the EFT statement-due job gains a manual override mode that runs only the notification step or only the overdue step for a chosen date and account, plus related fixes to due-date calculation and notification message type.
task: Operations staff need to manually trigger individual parts of the scheduled EFT statement-due job instead of always running everything at once. When the job is invoked, allow an optional action (either sending payment reminder/due notifications, or marking unpaid invoices as overdue), a date to emulate the job running on, and an optional account to limit it to; with no account it should apply across the environment, and with no action the job should behave as it does today. While doing this, make sure the statement payment due date is treated as the last day of the month following the statement period rather than simply one month after the period end. Also make sure that 'payment due' notifications (not only overdue ones) are sent as the due-notification email type rather than as a reminder. Document how to use these overrides in the developer notes.

subject: 21519 - Rework partner disbursement job so it works with multiple link and unlinking (#1637)
reason: The commit is one coherent rework of the partner disbursement journal job: it now covers the new per-transaction disbursement records alongside the legacy invoice-based ones, and it moves the invoice selection helpers that the non-government payables job relied on.
task: The nightly job that builds journal voucher files to pay out partners' shares of fees must also handle the newer per-transaction disbursement records, which are created when EFT payments are linked and unlinked. A single invoice can now be disbursed and reversed several times, and the old invoice-level status flag cannot track that. Gather both the legacy invoice-based disbursements and the pending partner disbursement records, grouped by fee distribution code. Write a credit and debit line for each item, flipping the direction for reversals. Use a flow-through identifier that combines the invoice and the disbursement record so repeated entries stay distinct. After upload, mark each item as uploaded, record when it was processed, and link it to the journal header with the correct link type. Only include partners flagged for partner disbursements, and skip distribution codes that are stopped from journal export. Keep the separate non-government payables file working by giving it its own invoice selection logic.

subject: Small fixes and tweaks for partner reversals (#1775)
reason: The commit is one coherent behavior change: it centralizes partner disbursement creation and reversal for EFT invoices, cancelling pending rows instead of adding duplicate reversals, creating disbursements when credits fully pay an invoice, and renaming the pending status with a data migration.
task: Partner disbursements for EFT invoices are being recorded inconsistently. Duplicate payment entries can appear when an invoice is created and later paid from credits. Reversals are always added as new entries, even when the original disbursement was never sent to the partner. Change the payment service so it adds a disbursement entry when an EFT invoice is created or becomes fully paid by applying short name credits, but only if no active non-reversal entry already exists. When an invoice is cancelled or its statement payment is reversed, cancel the pending disbursement if the nightly distribution job has not yet picked it up; otherwise add a reversal entry, and log an error if there is nothing to reverse or a reversal already exists. Also rename the 'waiting for receipt' status to a clearer 'waiting for the job' status, migrate existing records to it, and update the partner distribution job to pick up records in the new status.

subject: 21536 - Passing short Name Id parameter to find refunds (#1783)
reason: A single coherent feature that adds filtering of EFT short name refund listings by short name, threaded through the request parsing, service and data query layers.
task: When staff look up EFT refunds in the payment API, they can currently filter only by refund status, so the list shows refunds for every short name at once. Add support for an optional short name identifier on the refund listing request so that only refunds belonging to that EFT short name are returned. The existing comma-separated status filter should keep working, and both filters can be supplied together. This lets the short name detail screen show only the refunds relevant to that short name.

subject: Small tweaks for EFT patch approve declined route + Add in get route for refund (#1785)
reason: The changes form one coherent improvement to the EFT short name refund approval workflow: a new retrieval endpoint, a more lenient approve/decline update, and numeric serialization fixes that support it.
task: In the payment API, staff working with EFT short name refunds need to view a single refund request by its identifier. Add a way to fetch one refund, available to both refund requesters and refund approvers, that returns not found when the refund does not exist. When an approver approves or declines a pending refund, a comment should be optional, and any existing comment or decline reason should be kept rather than wiped if the update leaves them out. An unrecognized target status should be rejected with an error instead of being silently accepted. Refund records returned by the API should report numeric fields such as identifiers and amounts as real numbers rather than strings.

subject: Tweaks for send_email (#1786)
reason: The commit fixes EFT refund handling in the payment API: notification recipients are now passed as proper lists, and refund lookups now combine their filters correctly.
task: EFT refund notification emails in the payment API are not reaching recipients reliably. Approver addresses are passed to the email sender as one comma-joined string, and the client's refund address is passed as a bare string, when the sender expects a list of individual addresses. Change this so the approver lookup returns a list of addresses, including when a feature-flag override supplies a comma-separated list for testing, and so the client's address is wrapped in a list before sending. Also, when staff look up EFT refunds by both status and short name, only the last filter is applied; make the filters combine so both criteria narrow the results.

subject: 23942 - Small tweaks to invoice creation flow for skipPayment - for STRR/NRO and other various sandbox users (#1791)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: an environment-gated option to skip payment on invoice creation, mark the invoice paid and release it downstream, touching config, the request schema and the payment service.
task: In development, test and sandbox environments, some callers (for example the short-term rental registry and name request teams) need to create invoices without going through a real payment step. Let a payment request include an optional flag asking to skip payment. When the flag is set and the environment has explicitly enabled this behaviour through a configuration setting that is off by default, the invoice should be marked as paid in full right away, and the usual payment-completed notification should be sent downstream so the requesting system proceeds as if payment succeeded. Otherwise, the normal invoice completion flow should run unchanged, and production must never honour the flag unless the setting is enabled.

subject: 23154 partial refunds (#1792)
reason: The commit implements one coherent feature: completing partial refunds for credit card payments, with validation, tracking against the invoice, and automated confirmation that the refund was posted to the ledger.
task: Partial refunds on credit card (direct pay) invoices need to work end to end. When staff request a partial refund, the payment API should check that each refunded line belongs to the invoice. It should also check that each amount is non-negative and no larger than the matching fee portion of that line (filing, future effective, service or priority fees). The invoice should stay in a paid state, record the refunded amount as the sum of the partial lines rather than the full total, and stamp a refund date so a second refund is rejected. Each partial refund record should be linked directly to its invoice, with existing records backfilled, and should track when it was posted to the general ledger. The scheduled automated refund job should then poll the payment processor for these invoices and mark the partial refund records as posted once the processor reports completion. The email-sending helper the jobs use should come from the shared payment API library instead of a local copy.

subject: 19361 - Add refund status to routing slip (#1793)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: it adds a separate refund-tracking status to routing slips, makes it searchable, updatable and set during refund approval, and renames the final refund state.
task: Finance staff need to track a routing slip's refund after it has been approved, separately from the slip's main lifecycle status. Add a new refund progress indicator to routing slips with the values processing, processed, and cheque undeliverable. Store it in the database and return it in routing slip responses. Make it filterable in routing slip search, and allow staff to change it through the existing routing slip update endpoint with a new update action. When a refund decision is recorded, set the indicator to processing, or clear it if the refund was rejected and the slip goes back to active. Also rename the final 'refund completed' slip status to 'refund processed' everywhere, including existing data and the allowed status transitions.

subject: 20346 - Refactor Oracle to point at Datawarehouse instead of CPRD (#1804)
reason: The commit is one coherent behavior change: the BCOL refund confirmation job now reads refund billing records from a PostgreSQL financial data warehouse instead of the legacy Oracle database.
task: The nightly job that confirms BC Online refunds currently looks up refunded billing records by connecting directly to the legacy Oracle registry database. That direct dependency is being retired. Change the job to read the same refund billing records (entries recorded as negative-quantity reversals) from the financial data warehouse, which is a PostgreSQL instance hosted on Cloud SQL. The connection must work both through the Cloud SQL connector when deployed and over a plain host and port connection locally. Replace the Oracle connection settings and driver with data warehouse settings sourced from the secrets vault. Because the old per-query limit no longer applies, the batch size for invoice lookups can be increased.

subject: Sentry fixes + Disbursement job fix (#1811)
reason: The commit bundles unrelated changes (a disbursement job filter fix, an API guard for an undefined account number, a reconciliation empty-amount guard, and broad formatting changes), so it is a grab bag rather than one coherent behavior change.

subject: 20767 - Put in additional_headers for reverse proxy (#1813)
reason: The commit makes one coherent change: every outbound call from the payment API and the payment jobs to the CFS and PayBC services now sends a configurable shared-secret header so the calls can pass through a reverse proxy; the few formatting edits are incidental.
task: The calls we make to the provincial finance systems (the CFS accounts-receivable service and the PayBC payment service) are moving behind a reverse proxy. That proxy only lets a request through if it carries a shared secret in a custom header. Add a configurable secret, read from the environment, and send it as an extra request header on every outbound call to these systems. This covers token requests, customer/party, account and site creation and lookups, invoices, receipts, adjustments, credit memos and payment status checks. Apply it both in the payment API and in the scheduled payment jobs that check direct-pay payment details, post revenue distributions and handle automated refunds.

subject: 24111-EFT Federal Payments (#1814)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: incoming federal government EFT deposits in the bank reconciliation file now get their own uniquely generated short names, backed by a database sequence and a flag on the short name record.
task: The bank's daily EFT deposit file now includes deposits from the federal government. Every one of these deposits carries the same generic description, so today they all collapse into a single short name and cannot be told apart. When the payment queue's EFT reconciliation sees one of these federal deposits, it should create a brand-new EFT short name for that transaction. The name should be the generic federal description plus a unique number from a database sequence, and the short name should be marked as system-generated. These generated short names are always mapped to accounts manually, so the automatic step that applies pending payments from linked accounts should skip them.

subject: 20767 - More additional header changes (#1815)
reason: The commit makes one coherent change: it reworks how outbound calls to the provincial finance/payment systems authenticate with the reverse proxy, across the payment API, the payment jobs and the payment queue, and it adds the header to job calls that were missing it.
task: Outbound calls to the government finance system and the PayBC/direct-pay endpoints now go through a reverse proxy that expects a connector authorization value in a custom header. Replace the old proxy secret setting with a new connector-auth setting everywhere that header is sent: the payment API, the scheduled payment jobs, and the payment queue listener. Wire the new value into each service's secret/vault environment configuration. Also make sure the job that refreshes bank names on pre-authorized debit accounts sends this header when it reads and updates bank details in the finance system, since it currently bypasses it.

subject: 24454 - EFT TDI17 Processing updates (#1830)
reason: The commit is one coherent change to how the payment queue classifies incoming EFT deposit records: description patterns move into configuration, unmatched records get a fallback rule, and stored trailer totals are removed.
task: When the payment queue processes the bank's daily EFT deposit file, the description prefixes that mark a line as a wire transfer or an EFT payment are currently hard-coded. Make both lists of prefixes configurable per environment as comma-separated values. Classify each line by the first configured prefix it starts with, and strip that prefix to get the payer name. Any deposit that matches no prefix should still be handled: treat it as an EFT with an auto-generated short name, instead of using the special-cased federal payment rule. Processing should stop and report an error if the location filter or either prefix list is missing from configuration, and we no longer need to store the file trailer's detail count and deposit total on the EFT file record.

subject: 23620 - Get Transactions Query Optimization  (#1823)
reason: A single, coherent performance change to the transaction search query: it reshapes the query, runs the count and the page fetch concurrently, and replaces the JSON details search with a path-based match.
task: The account transactions search in the payment API is too slow for accounts with many invoices, especially when users filter by line item description or by invoice details. Make that search faster. Fetch only the columns the transaction listing needs, from one shared joined query. Run the total-count query and the current-page query at the same time instead of one after the other. Change the case-insensitive filtering on invoice details labels and values so it no longer has to expand the details array into extra rows, and use a native JSON path match instead. Search results, pagination, and totals must stay exactly the same as before.

subject: 24695 - EFT add cas supplier site - backend changes (#1848)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature that captures a CAS supplier site for EFT short names and EFT refunds and uses it in the accounts-payable refund file instead of a fixed configured location.
task: EFT refunds are currently sent to the government's accounts-payable system with a single fixed supplier location for every recipient. Finance staff need to record a CAS supplier site alongside the existing CAS supplier number. The supplier site should be stored on each EFT short name, editable through the short name update endpoint, and returned in short name listings. It must also be a required field when submitting an EFT refund request and saved with the refund. The nightly AP refund job should then write each refund's own supplier number and supplier site into the header, invoice line and comment records of the AP feed file, rather than using a global configured location.

subject: 24335 -EFT Refund fixes (#1851)
reason: The commit is a cohesive set of EFT short-name refund fixes: it enforces a separation-of-duties rule on refund approval and exposes the refund-related supplier and contact details in short-name summaries.
task: In the payment service, a staff member must not be able to approve an EFT short-name refund that they submitted themselves. If the approver is the same person who created the refund request, reject the approval with a forbidden error. The refund record should rely on the standard audit fields for who created it, not a separate duplicate field. Also, the EFT short-name summary listing should include each short name's CAS supplier number, CAS supplier site, and contact email, so staff can review refund payee details without opening each short name.

subject: Fix notebook report poetry (#1853)
reason: The commit moves the notebook report job from pip requirements to Poetry, adds Docker/Makefile tooling, and applies black/isort reformatting, with no change to how the job behaves.

subject: 24491 - Pay documents route (#1855)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: an authenticated endpoint that returns a static payment document as a PDF, generated through the existing report service.
task: Account holders need to be able to download the instructions for paying by electronic funds transfer as a PDF straight from the payment service. Add an authenticated endpoint to the payment API that takes a document type as a query parameter. It should render the matching document through the report generation service, with page numbers, and return it as a PDF attachment with a sensible file name. The download filename header must be readable by browser clients. For now only the EFT instructions document is supported; a missing or unrecognized document type should return a bad-request error. Allow report requests to the report service to be made without template variables, since static documents like this one don't need any.

subject: 21559 - Fix notebook so it's more consistent, also make it so the queries wor… (#1854)
reason: The commit is a coherent fix to the monthly partner reconciliation report: it uses a correct previous-calendar-month window in Pacific time, includes refunds and reversals, and centralizes report-service configuration, with some incidental cleanup.
task: The monthly reconciliation report emailed to partner ministries (court services, vital statistics, property tax, environmental remediation) is inconsistent. It uses a rolling window relative to today rather than the previous calendar month, and it only picks up fully paid, completed transactions. Change it so both the payments section and the disbursement section cover exactly the first through last day of the previous month, computed in Pacific time and converted to UTC for the queries. Also include transactions that were credited, refunded, cancelled or had refunds requested, and disbursements that were reversed in that window. Show refund and reversal dates, statuses and a subtotal excluding service fees, and format amounts and counts with thousands separators. The disbursed CSV should be named by month rather than by day, and the report-service URL and service-account credentials should be read from the job's central configuration instead of directly from the environment.

subject: More changes for notebook report
reason: The commit is one coherent change to how the monthly partner reconciliation report job produces and emails disbursement reconciliation files, including when the monthly run happens.
task: The monthly reconciliation report sent to partners should include a disbursement reconciliation spreadsheet only for partners whose payments we disburse (currently the court services and vital statistics partners). That list of partners should be configurable through the environment instead of being hard-coded. For those partners the disbursement spreadsheet must always be generated and attached, showing a 'no data retrieved' note when there is nothing to report. Other partners should no longer have a missing disbursement file referenced in their email. The monthly reports should also run whenever the monthly job is triggered, rather than depending on a configured day of the month, and the duplicate extra run on the 1st of the month should be removed.

subject: Enhance logging to print traceback (#1858)
reason: The commit makes one coherent observability change: the SFTP polling jobs and the payment queue worker now log full stack traces with caught errors, plus one minor config tweak.
task: When the scheduled jobs that poll the SFTP server for incoming payment files (the CAS settlement, EFT deposit, and CGI feedback pollers) hit an error while processing a file, they currently log only the bare exception message. That makes production failures very hard to diagnose. The payment queue's event worker has a similar gap: it swallows errors so the message is still acknowledged, but its log line does not capture the underlying error in a clear, consistent format. Update these error handlers so each failure is logged as a single structured entry containing both the error message and the full stack trace. The goal is that operators can find the root cause directly from the logs.

subject: 24811 - Add in new excludeCounts search filter while maintaining backwards compatability (#1861)
reason: The commit is a single coherent feature: an opt-in search mode for purchase history that skips the costly total count and reports whether more results exist, while the old counted behavior stays as it was.
task: Searching an account's transaction (purchase) history in the payment API is slow because every page request also computes the total number of matching records. Add an optional flag in the search request body that lets a caller skip the total count. When the flag is set, return only the requested page plus an indicator of whether more results exist beyond it, computed by fetching one extra row rather than counting. When the flag is not set, the existing behavior that returns a total must keep working unchanged, so staff tools and CSV/report exports are not broken. While doing this, move the stamping of the caller's product code onto the search filter out of the data layer and into the service layer, and validate the request body before rejecting an undefined account number.

subject: Notebook - Add in STRR (#1857)
reason: The commit coherently onboards the short-term rental registry as a new partner in the reporting job: it adds the partner to monthly reconciliation and disbursement reporting, adds its statement address details, and widens the payment methods the reconciliation covers.
task: Add the Short-Term Rental Registry as a partner in the scheduled partner reporting job so it gets monthly reconciliation and disbursement summaries, with its own configurable recipient list. Its statements should show the Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs mailing address (PO Box 9844, Stn Prov Govt, 4th Floor, 614 Humboldt Street, Victoria BC V8W 1A4). This partner is paid by more than pre-authorized debit and electronic journal voucher, so the monthly reconciliation, disbursement and statement queries should also include electronic funds transfer and direct-pay transactions. The reconciliation summary should also list each invoice's line items, showing quantity, description and amount. Also fix the disbursement partner list setting so the environment variable name it reads is spelled correctly.

subject: Improve the reporting a bit, organize it, add more fields (#1864)
reason: The commit is one coherent improvement to the monthly partner reconciliation reports: it adds account, creator, folio and fee-code details to the reports, plus a small switch for running the report job locally without sending email.
task: Finance and partner teams find the monthly partner reconciliation reports produced by the payment reporting job too sparse to reconcile against. For each transaction, both the monthly summary and the disbursement breakdown should show the creator's display name and username, and the payer's account number and account name. They should also include the folio number, and each line item should list its quantity, filing type code, description and amount. The disbursement report should line up with the summary report by also showing the creation date, payment date, refund date and invoice status, and it should label the net amount as the disbursed amount. Developers also need a configuration option that stops the report job from emailing results, so it can be run safely on a local machine.

subject: 24652 - updates for KC group contact_centre_staff (#1865)
reason: A coherent authorization change that adds new fine-grained view roles so contact centre staff can read account transactions, statements and statement settings in the payment API.
task: Contact centre staff need read-only access to customer account financial information in the payment service without being granted full editor rights. Introduce three new view permissions: viewing statements, viewing statement settings, and viewing account transactions. Allow users who have one of these permissions, as an alternative to the editor role, to do the following for an account: list and download its statements, read its statement settings and statement notification settings, and search or export its own purchase history (transactions). Searching transactions across all organizations should still require both the editor role and the existing view-all-transactions permission.

subject: Override Sandbox DIRECT_PAY / ONLINE_BANKING to PAD payment method (#1868)
reason: The commit implements one coherent business rule about which payment methods are allowed in sandbox versus API-client contexts; the formatting tweaks are incidental.
task: In the sandbox environment, when a new payment account is created with direct credit card payment or online banking as its payment method, the payment service should quietly switch it to pre-authorized debit and log that it did so, because those methods can't be used in sandbox. Also, when an external API-client user (identified by a dedicated API-user role) creates an invoice outside the sandbox, the payment service should reject direct credit card payment and online banking as invalid payment methods. Add support for recognizing this API-user role in the current user's context so the service can apply the rule.

subject: 24871  - Add route return valid payment method for product (#1866)
reason: A single coherent feature: store the allowed payment methods for each product and expose them through a new lookup endpoint in the payment API.
task: Front ends need a way to ask the payment API which payment methods are allowed for a given product, so they can stop hard-coding that list. Record the allowed payment methods for each product alongside the existing filing-type reference data, and seed the current rules. For example, business filings accept pre-authorized debit, credit card, electronic funds transfer, journal voucher, online banking, BC Online drawdown and internal payments, while most other products allow a smaller subset, and anything unlisted allows only internal payments. Add a public, CORS-enabled lookup under the code-table endpoints that returns a map of product to its allowed payment methods: all products when none is specified, or just the requested product (empty when it is unknown).

subject: 24990 & 24991 - Use Google buckets instead of SFTP (#1867)
reason: A single coherent change: the payment jobs stage their journal voucher files in a cloud storage bucket, and the FTP poller job picks them up from the bucket and transfers them to the government finance system over SFTP.
task: Today the payment jobs connect directly to the government finance system's SFTP server to deliver the journal voucher files they generate, along with each file's trigger file. Change this so the payment jobs drop both files into a 'processing' area of a shared Google Cloud Storage bucket instead, authenticating with a service account supplied through configuration. Then add a new run mode to the FTP poller job. In that mode it downloads any files waiting in the processing area, uploads them to the finance system's SFTP directory, and moves them into a 'processed' area of the bucket. This keeps SFTP credentials and connectivity in a single job, and the existing copy saved to object storage for record keeping should continue unchanged.

subject: Remove unused code, add in check for system - service accounts have a… (#1872)
reason: The commit bundles three unrelated changes (removing the EFT payment-method feature flag, removing the partial-refund feature flag, and exempting system service accounts from the API-user payment-method restriction) plus a dependency lock bump, so it is a grab bag rather than one coherent behavior change.

subject: 23812 - EFT TDI17 deposit/transaction date timezone (#1878)
reason: Despite dependency noise, the core is one coherent fix: EFT deposit and transaction dates from the bank's TDI17 file are interpreted as Pacific time, stored timezone-aware in UTC with existing data migrated, and the short-name summary search and output adjusted to use full timestamps.
task: EFT deposit and transaction dates read from the bank's daily TDI17 deposit file are in Pacific (Vancouver) local time, but we currently save them as if they were UTC with no timezone information, so times shown to staff are off by several hours. Update the payment queue's EFT file parser so both the deposit date-time and the transaction date are treated as Vancouver local time and converted to UTC. Store these values timezone-aware in the database, and add a migration that changes the column types and corrects existing rows by reinterpreting them from Vancouver time to UTC. In the payment API's EFT short name summary endpoint, accept the 'payment received' start and end filters as full ISO date-time strings and compare them against the exact timestamp instead of only the calendar date. Return the last payment received date as a full ISO timestamp that includes the timezone offset.

subject: 25334 - EFT Statement payment (#1882)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: EFT credits can be applied to or cancelled against a single statement, and the linked-accounts view now lists each owing statement with its pending payments; the refactoring exists to support this.
task: Staff currently can only apply a short name's unapplied EFT credit to all of a linked account's outstanding statements at once, and can only cancel pending EFT payments for the whole account. Allow staff to target one specific statement when applying or cancelling EFT credit. If the chosen statement does not belong to the account, reject the request with a clear validation error. Also, when listing the accounts linked to an EFT short name, include for each account its statements that still have a balance owing, showing the amount owing and the count and total of payments already pending on each. This lets staff choose which statement to pay.

subject: 25223 - update EFT emails to point to pay web (#1891)
reason: A single coherent behavior change: EFT notification emails (overpayment and refund approval/decision) now link to the short name details page in the separate payment web app instead of the account management web app.
task: EFT-related notification emails currently send staff to the short name details page in the account management web app, but that page now lives in the standalone payment staff web app under its EFT section. Update the links in the EFT overpayment notification sent by the payment batch jobs and in the EFT refund emails (pending-approval notice to approvers and the approved/declined notices) sent by the payment API so they point to the payment web app's EFT short name details page. Add configuration for the payment web app's base URL to both the payment API and the payment jobs, and wire it into their deployment secrets so each environment links to the correct site.

subject: More changes for revenue letter, fix spacing, allow override (#1892)
reason: The commit is one coherent change to the monthly partner reconciliation report job: the reporting period can be overridden, filenames follow that period, the revenue letter's month text is trimmed, and the email attaches whatever partner files were generated.
task: The monthly partner reconciliation report job always computes the previous month from today's date, so it can't be rerun for an earlier period. Add an optional setting that lets operators supply a substitute 'current date', and derive the reporting window from it. The generated summary and disbursement CSV names should use the year-month of that reporting window rather than today's date. Also trim stray whitespace from the month name shown in the partner revenue letter. Finally, the notification email to each partner should attach every report file actually generated for that partner, instead of a hard-coded list that currently drops the disbursement file.

subject: Remove feature flag for enable eft (#1903)
reason: The commit is one coherent behavior change: it removes the EFT payment-method feature flag and makes the formerly gated EFT behavior unconditional in the payment API endpoint, account update logic and statement notification job; the lock file changes are incidental dependency repointing.
task: Electronic funds transfer (EFT) is now fully rolled out as a payment method, so the feature toggle that gated it should be retired and EFT behavior should always be active. When a payment is made against an account, the payment service should always honor the options to pay the outstanding balance and to include invoices of all statuses, instead of ignoring them unless the toggle is on. When an account's method of payment is updated, the special handling for switching to or from EFT should always run. The scheduled statement notification job should always send the EFT-specific statement notification, which includes the account's total amount due, for EFT accounts, rather than marking those notifications as skipped when the toggle is off. Remove the toggle from the local flag configuration of the API, the queue service and the jobs.

subject: 24664 - Adding sbc-finance to PAD locking email (#1905)
reason: Despite the visible lock-file churn, the commit subject describes one coherent behavior change: also sending the PAD account-locking notification to the finance team.
task: When a pre-authorized debit (PAD) account is locked because a debit failed, for example for insufficient funds, the notification email currently goes only to the account's administrators. The finance team also needs to know about these locks so they can follow up on outstanding balances. Change the account-locking notification so the finance team's shared mailbox also receives a copy. Make the finance mailbox address configurable, and keep all existing recipients.

subject: Fix secret for topics (#1921)
reason: The commit is one coherent fix: it makes the per-product payment notification topics configurable, with sensible defaults, in both the payment queue service and the payment jobs so they can publish payment completion events, and it raises the online banking publish log line to info.
task: The payment queue service and the scheduled payment jobs need to publish payment-completed events to the downstream product topics: the business registry, name requests, and short-term rental registration. Right now they don't have these destination topics in their settings. Make each of the three topics configurable from the environment in both services. Business and name requests should fall back to their standard development topics, and short-term rentals should fall back to the business topic when no value is given. Also, when reconciliation publishes a payment event for an online banking payment, log it at a level that shows up in normal production logs so we can trace these events.

subject: 26465 - Backend changes to support new EFT refunds (#1927)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: EFT short name refunds can now be paid by mailed cheque as well as by direct deposit, with new refund method, mailing address and cheque status data, plus validation that depends on the chosen method.
task: Staff need to refund unapplied EFT credit on a short name either by electronic deposit to a CAS supplier or by a mailed cheque. When staff create a short name refund in the payment API, they must choose a refund method. For electronic refunds the CAS supplier number and site are required. For cheque refunds the recipient's name and full mailing address (street, city, province/region, postal code, country, plus optional additional street line and delivery instructions) are required instead. Store these details on the refund record, letting the CAS supplier number be empty for cheque refunds. Reject requests that are missing required fields, have a zero or negative amount, or use an unknown method. Let staff update a refund's cheque status separately, without having to resend its approval status, and reuse the existing routing slip cheque refund statuses for this.

subject: 26465 - PAY-JOBS - EFT Refund cheque support (#1930)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: the payment jobs' accounts-payable file generation now supports refunding EFT short-name balances by mailed cheque as well as by direct deposit, with supplier, distribution, terms and address handling chosen per refund flow.
task: The nightly payment job that builds accounts-payable batch files for the provincial finance system currently pays out EFT short-name refunds only by electronic funds transfer to the recipient's own supplier number and site. Finance staff now also need to refund EFT balances by mailed cheque. Use the refund method recorded on each EFT refund to decide how it is paid out. Cheque refunds should be issued under the government's general cheque supplier and site, with no 'Immediate' payment terms. Each cheque refund should include a mailing-address override record, built from the refund's entity name and address, because only that address appears on the cheque envelope. Every EFT refund, whether by cheque or by transfer, should also carry a comment line with the short name and the refund comment, because that text is printed with the cheque. Count all these records in the batch control totals. Existing routing-slip cheque refunds and the non-government transfer disbursements must keep producing the same output, so the formatting rules should be driven by the type of payout flow rather than by the type of file being generated.

subject: 26076-26073-26075-EFT Refund updates (#1931)
reason: The commit is one coherent change to the EFT refund update workflow: it splits approving or declining a refund from updating its cheque status, adjusts the role permissions for each, and includes the refund method in notification emails.
task: In the payment service, staff who manage EFT accounts but are not refund approvers should be able to update the cheque status of an EFT short name refund. Approving or declining a refund must still require the refund approver role. When a request sets a cheque status, treat it as a cheque status update only. That update is allowed only once the refund has been approved, and any other case should be rejected with a clear bad-request error. A decline reason should only be recorded when the refund is actually declined. The refund notification emails should carry the refund method, so the client email says the refund was issued to them by cheque when the method is cheque, and to their original payment method otherwise.

subject: Change error, only allow DIRECT_PAY for partial refund (#1937)
reason: The commit changes a refund business rule so partial refunds are allowed only for invoices paid by direct credit-card payment, replacing the old partner-disbursement check and renaming the error to match.
task: In the payment service, partial refunds are currently blocked only when the invoice's product type pays out to partners. That check does not reflect what the downstream systems can actually support. Change the rule so a partial refund is accepted only when the invoice was paid by direct online credit-card payment, and reject it for every other payment method. When a partial refund is rejected, return a bad-request error whose code and message say that partial refunds are not supported for that payment method, instead of mentioning disbursements.

subject: 27109 - Allow sandbox users to use account-ui to update their pad details (#1941)
reason: A single coherent change: sandbox behavior in the payment API now keys off a deployment-level environment setting instead of a token role, and the external bank system calls for pre-authorized debit (PAD) bank validation and updates are mocked in sandbox so sandbox users can manage PAD details.
task: Sandbox users cannot update their pre-authorized debit bank details through the account management UI. Today the payment service only recognizes sandbox through a special role on the caller's token or a query flag that requires a sandbox-creation role, and regular account UI users have neither. Change the payment service so it decides it is running in sandbox from a configurable deployment environment name (defaulting to local), and drop the token-role check entirely. Everywhere sandbox behavior applies (skipping invoice creation with the government finance system, auto-completing payments, allowing restricted payment methods, blocking certain methods at account creation), use the environment check instead. In sandbox, also skip the real calls to the government finance system: bank account validation should return a mocked successful response that echoes back the submitted bank details, and updating PAD bank details should use a placeholder payment instrument instead of calling the finance system.

subject: 19543  - ONLINE BANKING / PAD Partial Refund as Credit (#1942)
reason: A single coherent feature that extends partial refunds to online banking and pre-authorized debit payments by issuing account credit, along with a configurable per-payment-method allowance.
task: Today the payment service only accepts partial refunds for invoices paid by direct credit card payment, and any other payment method is rejected. Extend partial refunds to online banking and pre-authorized debit invoices. For these methods, the refunded portion should not go back to the bank. Instead it should be issued as a credit memo in the financial system and added to the account's credit balance. Validate each refunded line so the amount is not negative and does not exceed that line's total, or its service fees when only service fees are being refunded. Reject partial refunds on invoices that are not yet paid with a clear error. The invoice should stay paid if only part of the total was refunded and become credited only when the full amount is returned. Which payment methods allow partial refunds should be configurable data stored per payment method, not hard-coded. Enable it for direct pay, online banking and pre-authorized debit.

subject: 23520 - Handle Continuation Draft States (#696)
reason: The commit is one coherent change to how continuation-in applications appear on the business dashboard across their draft, approved, change-requested and pending states, with only an incidental version bump.
task: Update the business dashboard so continuation-in applications show the right wording and actions at each stage of staff review of their authorization. A fresh continuation draft should offer a single 'Begin Continuation' action, whether or not a name request is attached. Once staff approve the authorization, the to-do item should show the name request's approval and expiry and its details, and offer a Resume button so the applicant can finish. When staff request changes, show the name request approval line and the message 'BC Registries staff require the following changes to your authorization documentation', with the staff comment on a grey background. In the pending section and items, drop the 'paid / filed by' wording in favour of a simpler 'Submitted on' date and a plain 'Pending' heading, since these filings are not necessarily paid at that point.

subject: Fix 23520 - Dashboard Updates for Continuation States (#697)
reason: The commit is one coherent behavior change: it updates how continuation-in filings are labelled and described across their lifecycle states (draft, awaiting review, change requested, approved, rejected, future effective) on the business dashboard.
task: Update the business dashboard so continuation-in filings read correctly at every stage. While the filing is a draft, awaiting staff review, or has changes requested, call it a Continuation Authorization rather than a Continuation Application. In those states the to-do and pending items should show who submitted it and when, plus the approved name request and its expiry wording, and should load the name request for pending filings too. Approved items should say the continuation authorization was approved, should only show name request details when a name request exists and hasn't expired, and should open the business in its temporary-business context instead of the completed-business view. Change-requested and pending items should use friendlier staff-review wording, a 5-business-day review estimate, and registry contact information. Rejected and future-effective continuation entries in the filing history should say "continuation" and "submitted" rather than "incorporation" and "paid".

subject: 22639 - Update Certify Section Wording (#704)
reason: The commit makes one coherent change to the certification statement shown on filings: staff get third-person wording, the generic fallback becomes 'business', and the per-entity display names that fed the statement are removed for the corporation types.
task: Reword the certification statement that users must check before submitting a filing in the filing UI. When a staff member files on a client's behalf, the statement should be in the third person: the named certifier certifies that they know the business and are authorized to file. Everyone else should keep the first-person 'I certify' form, with slightly reworded grammar. When no entity description is available, the statement should refer generically to the business rather than to an association. Also stop supplying the special descriptive names (for example the benefit company or unlimited liability company label) that the corporation business types currently use in this statement, so those companies fall back to the standard wording.

subject: 24657 - Notice of Withdrawal filing (#707)
reason: The commit adds one coherent feature: a new staff-only Notice of Withdrawal filing page in the business dashboard, with its routing, components, filing-history recognition and per-entity fee/certify configuration.
task: Add a new staff-only Notice of Withdrawal filing to the business dashboard so registry staff can withdraw a previously submitted future-effective record. The page should show the record being withdrawn (its filing type, filing number and effective date and time). It should also collect an optional court order number and let staff indicate whether the record was filed as part of a plan of arrangement. If the plan-of-arrangement option is checked, the court order number becomes required, and staff can then also mark that some provisions of the arrangement have already come into effect. The page must include document delivery, certification and staff payment sections, show an access-restricted dialog with a return-to-dashboard option to non-staff users, and support saving drafts, resuming drafts and submitting. Every business type should get a fee and certification text for this filing citing section 427 of the Business Corporations Act. The filing history should recognize this new filing type, and the certification statement should show its leading 'Note:' as a bold label instead of embedding it in each filing's text.

subject: 24953 - Update NoW Filing Page (#708)
reason: The commit is one coherent rework of the Notice of Withdrawal filing page: it moves the plan-of-arrangement questions into the record-to-be-withdrawn section, blocks submission when arrangement terms have taken effect, and switches to the shared court order component.
task: On the Notice of Withdrawal filing page in the filing UI, move the plan of arrangement questions out of the court order section and into the section that describes the record being withdrawn. That section should ask whether the record is part of a plan of arrangement and, only if it is, whether at least one of the arrangement's terms has taken effect. If terms have taken effect, show a red warning box explaining that all related records must be withdrawn before any provisions take effect, and prevent the filing from being submitted. The court order section should use the standard shared court order and plan of arrangement input used on other filings, with an explanatory note and an optional court order number. Save and reload the two new answers as part of the withdrawal data sent to the legal API, drop the old 'arrangement has come into effect' court order value, read drafts from the correctly named withdrawal object, and return to the business dashboard when the identifier of the filing being withdrawn is missing or invalid.

subject: 25294 - Submit NoW for Bootstrap Filing (#712)
reason: The commit is one coherent feature: it lets a Notice of Withdrawal be submitted against a bootstrap (not-yet-completed) filing by populating the founding date, email and fallback legal name from the draft application, and by omitting empty values from the submitted payload.
task: Staff need to be able to file a Notice of Withdrawal against a future-effective bootstrap filing (an incorporation, amalgamation, continuation in or registration that has not yet completed), but submission currently fails because the temporary business is missing key details. When the filing UI loads a bootstrap filing, it should take the founding date from the filing's effective date and the business email from the application's contact point. It should also set a sensible legal name when there is no name request: 'Numbered Amalgamated Company' for amalgamations, and the numbered-company description for the entity type otherwise. In the withdrawal and the related out-filings (amalgamation out, continuation out and their consents), empty email or founding date values should be left out of the submitted filing rather than sent as blank strings, so the legal API's validation accepts them.

subject: 25190 - Court Order Filings (#714)
reason: The commit subject suggests a court-order feature, but the visible diff contains only the app version bump, the shared enums package bump and lockfile dependency churn, so no specific behavior change can be identified or described.

subject: 26495 - Correct Amalgamation Out Filing Typos and Labels (#733)
reason: The commit is one coherent fix to the amalgamation-out filing page: it corrects wording copied from continuation out, fixes draft-loading of the detail comment, and shows the business header on the amalgamation-out screens.
task: The amalgamation-out filing screen in the filing UI was cloned from the continuation-out screen and still shows continuation-out wording. The effective date section's heading, its date field label and its required-date error message all mention continuation out. The documents-delivery note and the unsaved-changes exit dialog do too. Update these so the amalgamation-out filing refers to amalgamation out, while the continuation-out filing keeps its current text. Also fix resuming a saved amalgamation-out draft, which fails to restore the detail comment because it reads the wrong section of the filing. Finally, show the business information header on the amalgamation-out and consent-to-amalgamate-out pages, as other filing pages already do.

subject: 27042 remove address fetch error (#744)
reason: The commit is one coherent fix: the office address change filing now tolerates businesses with missing or not-yet-entered registered/records office addresses instead of raising a fetch error.
task: When a user opens the standalone change-of-office-address filing for a business that has no registered or records office address on file, the filing UI currently treats the gap as a failure and shows a fetch error dialog. Change this so a missing address (including a not-found response from the legal API's addresses lookup) is handled gracefully. Show each empty delivery or mailing address as "(Not entered)" in the read-only view, and still let the user enter new addresses. Only a business type that requires a records office should keep a records office section when none is returned. Do not consider the records office to be the same as the registered office when the registered addresses are blank. Treat the form as valid when the records office inherits the registered office.
